artigo.texto: Business Follow Us on Google September 29, 2026 by Franca Ochigbo, Abuja FG approves carbon market framework, moves to establish approval criteria The Federal Government has taken steps to institutionalise Nigeria’s carbon market by approving a framework for its operation, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, Prof. Simon Uchenna Ortuanya, has said. Ortuanya, represented by Prof. Nnaemeka Chukwuone, spoke at the National Stakeholders Review and Validation Workshop on the draft Host Country Approval Criteria for Nigeria’s Carbon Market Operations, organised by the National Council on Climate Change in Abuja. He said the global carbon market offered countries opportunities to mobilise climate finance for greenhouse gas emission reduction and removal while supporting the transition to a low-carbon economy. According to him, the opportunities are particularly important for Nigeria as the country seeks to pursue economic growth, industrial development, energy access and poverty reduction while responding to climate change. “The approval represents an important step towards establishing a structured system for carbon market operations in the country. The next critical task is the reason why we are in this meeting, which is to ensure that the framework is supported by clear, practical and transparent host country approval criteria,” he said. Ortuanya said the criteria would guide the eligibility and assessment of carbon market projects while clarifying institutional responsibilities, measurement and reporting procedures, verification requirements, environmental and social safeguards, alignment with Nigeria’s nationally determined contributions, registry and transparency arrangements, and carbon accounting. He stressed the need for the criteria to protect Nigeria’s interests while remaining practical and predictable within the country’s regulatory environment. He said the proposed criteria were developed with research input from the University of Nigeria, adding that effective public policy should be based on credible research, evidence and stakeholder engagement. The Vice Chancellor said the participatory approach adopted for the workshop included technical sessions, stakeholder group discussions and plenary deliberations aimed at generating recommendations for refining and finalising the Host Country Approval criteria. He urged participants to examine the proposed project eligibility and assessment requirements and determine whether institutional roles and coordination arrangements were sufficiently clear. artigo.texto: Renesas Unveils Industry's First 650V GaN in Dual-Side Cooled 8x8mm Package for Megawatt-Scale AI Data Centers - Dual-side cooling (DSC) shrinks package footprint by 57% compared with TOLT, packing more power into space-constrained megawatt-scale racks. - One of the lowest on resistances in the 650V class, at 20 mΩ in an 8x8 mm package. - Single-source path to 800V designs with industry-standard PQFN footprint plus full controller, driver and MCU lineup. These solutions will be on display at OCP Global Summit in San Jose, CA ,October 12-15 . This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260930184285/en/ Built on its Gen IV Plus GaN architecture, the device is purpose-built for the megawatt-scale demands driving next-generation AI data centers supporting up to 700V operation. It targets the 800V DC/DC intermediate bus converter (IBC) stage that steps down to 48V, 12V or 6V, along with the battery backup (BBU) and capacitor bank (CBU) stages of the sidecar power rack. As rack power climbs from roughly 120 kW toward megawatt scale, space and heat have become critical factors in sustaining the power level. Unlike conventional top-side-cooled packages, the new device dissipates heat from both top and bottom, lowering top-side thermal impedance by 10%. Its 8 x 8mm PQFN footprint is also 57% smaller than the existing 10 x 15mm TOLT package. The device incorporates the full strength of Renesas Gen IV Plus 650V GaN technology: low gate charge and output capacitance, a built-in freewheeling diode with minimal reverse recovery and a high threshold voltage that runs without a negative gate bias. Engineers can drive it with a standard silicon gate driver, switch into the MHz frequency range to minimize passive components and cut overall BOM cost without requiring a specialized E-mode driver. "Customers building megawatt-scale AI data centers are running out of board space and thermal headroom before they hit their power limits," said The new dual-side-cooled (DSC) PQFN package is defined in collaboration with major AI infrastructure customers, enabling an industry-standard footprint for sourcing flexibility. When paired with Renesas AUX controllers, gate drivers and MCUs, the GaN device creates a one-stop-shop power solution for OEMs, ODMs and hyperscalers moving to 800V architectures. Renesas has already validated the approach in silicon. A 6kW, 800V-to-48V LLC DC transformer (DCX) reference design built on the new device and controlled by a Renesas RA6T3 MCU reaches a power density of 2.6 kW/in³ with per-module testing measuring full-load efficiency 0.21% higher than an equivalent TOLT-based board. The smaller package also saves PCB space and enables a better-matched layout across the FETs. 800V-to-12V and 6V DC/DC IBC reference designs also leverage the new DSC 8x8 platform, delivering similar enhanced performance, scalability and power density levels. Renesas will showcase the new TP65H020G4PLSGBD GaN device as part of its 800V power solutions at OCP Global Summit, Availability The TP65H020G4PLSGBD is sampling today. Mass production is planned for mid-2027. More information about Renesas GaN solutions is available at: renesas.com/gan-fets. Our power portfolio seamlessly attaches to our leading MCU, MPU, SoC and analog solutions, simplifying and accelerating the design process with hundreds of engineering-vetted Winning Combinations and innovative tools such as PowerCompass™ and PowerNavigator™ design software. artigo.texto: TORONTO, Sept. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Northland Power Inc. (“Northland” or the “Company”) (TSX: NPI) today announced the close of approximately PLN 500 million (CAD 185 million) in project financing for its Mieczysławów (200 MW / 800 MWh) and Kamionka (100 MW / 400 MWh) battery energy storage system (“BESS”) projects in Poland, both of which are currently under construction. The financing was secured with Canadian and Polish financial institutions and completes the funding structure for the projects. Both projects have also received grants totaling approximately PLN 280 million (CAD 105 million) from Poland’s National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management. Northland has already fulfilled its equity commitment for both projects using corporate cash and available funding. Total capital costs for Kamionka and Mieczysławów are estimated to be approximately PLN 1.0 billion (CAD 0.4 billion). “Securing financing for Kamionka and Mieczysławów completes the funding structure for both projects and marks another important milestone in Northland’s growth in Poland,” said Jeff Hart, Chief Financial Officer of Northland Power. “These projects demonstrate our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our ability to execute on projects. As demand for flexible grid infrastructure continues to grow, battery storage is an important part of our portfolio and a key driver of long-term value creation.” Kamionka and Mieczysławów remain on track, with commercial operations expected in early 2028 and mid-2028, respectively. Once fully operational, the projects are expected to contribute approximately $40 million to $50 million of combined annual Adjusted EBITDA. Acquired in November 2025 as late-stage, pre-construction projects, Northland has since advanced both projects through development, secured grant funding and project financing, and commenced construction. Together, the facilities will provide 300 MW / 1.2 GWh of battery storage capacity, with a portion of revenues contracted under 17-year inflation-indexed auction agreements and additional revenue opportunities through energy arbitrage and ancillary services markets. Once operational, Kamionka and Mieczysławów are expected to be among the first utility-scale standalone battery storage facilities operating in Poland. Together with Baltic Power, the projects further strengthen the Company’s presence in one of its core growth markets. The facilities will support grid reliability, increase system flexibility and help integrate Poland’s growing renewable energy generation. artigo.texto: Redata encontra fila de mais de 56 GW por energia para data centers EPE tenta separar projetos reais dos que podem não sair do papel; expansão já exige R$ 1,6 bilhão em novas obras de transmissão só em São Paulo A sanção do Redata colocou combustível em uma corrida por data centers que começa a esbarrar em um recurso mais difícil de encontrar do que terrenos: energia disponível para conectar os novos empreendimentos. O presidente da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), Thiago Prado, afirmou neste mês que já existem mais de 56 gigawatts (GW) em pedidos de acesso à rede feitos por projetos de data centers. O próprio executivo fez uma ressalva importante: uma parcela dessas iniciativas provavelmente não sairá do papel, e a estatal está procurando investidores para entender o grau de maturidade dos projetos antes de recomendar novas expansões da infraestrutura elétrica. A cifra mostra a velocidade com que o mapa mudou. Pouco mais de 60 dias depois da primeira versão do Redata, editada em setembro de 2025, a EPE havia registrado um salto de 19,8 GW para 26,2 GW apenas entre os projetos que protocolaram no Ministério de Minas e Energia pedidos de estudo para conexão à Rede Básica. Ou seja: naquele curto intervalo, surgiram 6,4 GW adicionais de demanda potencial. Agora transformado em lei, o Redata foi sancionado em 15 de setembro. O regime reduz a carga tributária sobre a compra e a importação de equipamentos de tecnologia utilizados nos centros de dados, incluindo a suspensão de PIS/Cofins, IPI e, em determinadas condições, Imposto de Importação. O objetivo é diminuir um dos custos que tornavam o Brasil menos competitivo para instalações voltadas a computação em nuvem, processamento de alto desempenho e inteligência artificial. O incentivo tributário, porém, resolve apenas uma parte da equação. A corrida pela tomada Grandes data centers são consumidores de eletricidade de escala industrial. E a velocidade de construção dessas instalações não necessariamente acompanha a expansão do sistema elétrico. Prado estima que uma grande unidade possa ser erguida em cerca de três anos, enquanto uma nova linha de transmissão pode levar aproximadamente cinco anos. É esse descompasso que começa a preocupar o planejamento do setor. São Paulo, que concentra a maior parcela do mercado brasileiro, dá a dimensão do problema. A EPE já recomendou aproximadamente R$ 1,6 bilhão em novos investimentos de transmissão no estado para liberar cerca de 4 GW de margem para novas conexões. Outros estudos podem acrescentar mais 5 GW de capacidade. E a pressão não está restrita ao estado. A estatal prepara estudos para viabilizar da ordem de 4 GW de novos projetos no Rio de Janeiro; analisa no Rio Grande do Sul empreendimento com demanda que pode chegar a 5 GW; e trabalha em soluções capazes de aumentar em outros 4 GW a capacidade de conexão de grandes cargas no Nordeste. Os números de pedidos de energia são muito maiores do que o mercado efetivamente em construção — justamente uma razão para a cautela da EPE. Levantamento da consultoria imobiliária JLL aponta atualmente 660 MW de data centers em construção no país, capazes de atrair cerca de US$ 17,4 bilhões em investimentos, além de outros 4.621 MW no pipeline. A taxa de vacância nacional está em apenas 4%, e 56% do estoque novo em construção já havia sido pré-locado. Energia limpa também entra na conta O próprio desenho do Redata transforma a disponibilidade de energia em peça central da escolha de onde construir. Para usufruir do regime, o data center terá de atender 100% de sua demanda elétrica com contratos de suprimento ou autoprodução provenientes de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão. A lei também estabelece limite de eficiência hídrica e obriga investimentos em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação. Parte dos detalhes ainda é remetida a regulamentação. Há ainda uma exigência de que pelo menos 10% da capacidade beneficiada seja destinada ao mercado brasileiro — obrigação que pode ser substituída, nos termos previstos pela lei e sua regulamentação, por investimentos adicionais em pesquisa e desenvolvimento O resultado é uma mudança na lógica da disputa imobiliária que acompanha o boom dos data centers. Não basta mais ter uma grande área disponível. O endereço valioso é aquele que combina terreno, fibra óptica e, principalmente, megawatts que possam efetivamente chegar ao empreendimento. Com o Redata reduzindo a barreira tributária para os equipamentos, é justamente essa disputa pela tomada que tende a definir quais dos dezenas de gigawatts hoje apresentados ao sistema elétrico virarão data centers de verdade.

artigo.texto: PARIS LA DÉFENSE--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 1, 2026-- Regulatory News: Arkema (Paris:AKE) continues to invest in the battery business value chain and announces a €10 million expansion project for its Global Battery Center of Excellence located in Oullins-Pierre-Bénite, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France. This investment reflects the Group's strategy of continuously strengthening its research capabilities in advanced materials for batteries within its global network of R&D laboratories covering the entire battery value chain. Following the inauguration in Normandy in September 2025 of a laboratory dedicated to solvent-free battery electrode manufacturing, as well as several investments in Asia and the Americas, this expansion further strengthens a particularly dense global R&D network, that combines the expertise developed in France with that of the Group’s research centers in China, South Korea, Japan and the United States. Thanks to this international organization, Arkema is accelerating the development of innovative solutions capable of addressing the technological and industrial challenges of next-generation batteries. Located at the heart of the Rhône-Alpes Research Center, the Battery Center of Excellence is entering a new phase of its development. Its footprint will be tripled, and its research infrastructure will be modernized, including notably a significant increase in the digitalization of R&D activities. This expansion will consolidate the role of this French center as Arkema’s global reference platform for the development of advanced materials serving both current batteries and the next generations under development. The project will enable the Group’s R&D teams to prepare for the future industrial standards of cell manufacturers and accelerate the integration of Arkema’s advanced materials into their production processes. By replicating their customers’ manufacturing conditions, researchers will be able to better anticipate implementation constraints and contribute to the development of more efficient batteries delivering greater energy density, faster charging times and enhanced safety. “This investment marks a major milestone in Arkema’s ambition to support the rapid evolution of the battery market. By strengthening our Battery Center of Excellence in France, we are equipping our global network and teams with state-of-the-art tools that will enable them to develop, in close collaboration with our customers, the materials that will contribute to the performance of tomorrow’s batteries,” said Armand Ajdari, Arkema’s Chief technology Officer. The implementation of this project has been made possible in particular through the support provided by the French Research Tax Credit (Crédit d’Impôt Recherche) and by the French State as part of the France 2030 program. Building on its unique set of expertise in materials science, Arkema offers a portfolio of first-class technologies to address ever-growing demand for new and more sustainable materials. With the ambition to become a world leader in Specialty Materials, the Group is structured into three complementary, resilient and highly innovative segments dedicated to Specialty Materials - Adhesive Solutions, Advanced Materials, and Coating Solutions - accounting for some 85% of Group sales in 2025, and a Primary Materials segment regrouping well-positioned large scale industrials activities. Arkema offers cutting-edge technological solutions to meet the challenges of, among other things, new energies, access to water, recycling, urbanization and mobility, and fosters a permanent dialogue with all its stakeholders. The Group reported sales of around €9.1 billion in 2025 and operates in some 55 countries with 20,700 employees worldwide. artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. FAW Group, GAIG Automobile Form Alliance FAW Group and Guangzhou Automobile Industry Group ("GAIG Automobile"), the controlling shareholder of GAC Group, signed a strategic cooperation framework agreement on September 29. The two state-owned automakers plan to strengthen coordination in assets and capital, technological innovation, and cross-regional industrial resources, drawing on their respective strengths in manufacturing, brands, global operations, and key automotive technologies. The agreement comes as GAC Group advances a major asset restructuring. Under a proposal disclosed on September 28, the listed automaker plans to acquire a 50% stake in FAW Toyota through a share issuance. The strategic partnership and the proposed transaction will move forward in parallel. China Unveils 2026-2030 Battery Plan China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and six other government departments have jointly released a plan for the new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), setting out development goals and key priorities. A key target is to achieve initial large-scale commercialization of all-solid-state batteries by 2030. The plan also calls for major advances in next-generation battery technologies, while targeting a cycle life of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries and product defect rates at the parts-per-billion level for leading manufacturers. The plan outlines 19 key tasks across five areas, including breakthroughs in all-solid-state battery industrialization, development of next-generation battery chemistries and a supply system centered on lithium-ion batteries alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries. It also calls for stronger battery recycling and the development of standards for emerging technologies. Beyond technology, China plans to promote the digital and green transformation of battery manufacturing and support battery companies expanding overseas. The policy also calls for international cooperation and measures to address overseas technical trade barriers, signaling an effort to strengthen China's battery industry across both technology development and global markets. XPeng's Carbon Credit Revenue Tops RMB 1 Billion XPeng has reportedly reached carbon credit deals with Porsche and several other international automakers covering emissions regulations in the EU, UK and Australia, generating more than RMB 1 billion ($140 million) in total revenue. XPeng's vice president confirmed that the reports were accurate, with the company expected to generate more than RMB 500 million in carbon credit revenue in 2026. The deals come as automakers face increasingly stringent emissions requirements in overseas markets. According to European Commission documents, Porsche has opted out of Volkswagen Group's internal CO₂ emissions pool and plans to form an independent open compliance pool for 2026–2027, with XPeng identified as a key partner. Under EU rules, automakers can form emissions pools and use surplus credits from low-emission manufacturers to offset excess emissions. XPeng's growing overseas sales are helping build its position as a potential carbon credit supplier. Its overseas deliveries topped 20,000 units in the second quarter, up 81% year on year, while overseas business accounted for more than 25% of revenue in the first half. From January to July, XPeng ranked first among Chinese new-energy brands in pure-electric sales in several European markets, including Norway, Denmark, France and Portugal. The development highlights a potential new revenue stream for Chinese automakers expanding overseas. As emissions regulations tighten globally, carbon credits are becoming an increasingly strategic asset, allowing automakers with strong EV sales to monetize their regulatory compliance advantages beyond vehicle sales themselves.

artigo.texto: Veja o resumo da notícia - A expansão da inteligência artificial pode gerar gargalos na produção de capacitores cerâmicos multicamadas (MLCCs). - A demanda por MLCCs deve crescer 4,3 vezes entre 2025 e 2030, enquanto a produção avança 10% a 15% ao ano. - Servidores de IA consomem 16 vezes mais energia que racks convencionais, exigindo mais MLCCs para estabilizar o sistema. - Uma placa de computação tradicional usa 2.500 MLCCs, enquanto arquiteturas de IA podem chegar a 12 mil unidades. - O mercado global de MLCCs pode superar US$ 30 bilhões até 2030, com IA e data centers representando 30% da receita. A expansão da inteligência artificial começa a pressionar um componente pouco conhecido, mas essencial para o funcionamento de servidores e data centers. Os capacitores cerâmicos multicamadas, chamados de MLCCs, podem se tornar um novo gargalo para a infraestrutura de IA nos próximos anos. Segundo relatório da Global X divulgado em setembro, a demanda por esses componentes pode crescer 4,3 vezes entre 2025 e 2030, com base em estimativa do Goldman Sachs Research. No entanto, a capacidade global de produção deve avançar entre 10% e 15% ao ano no mesmo período. Os MLCCs armazenam e liberam carga elétrica em frações de segundo. Além disso, ajudam a estabilizar a tensão e a filtrar ruídos nos circuitos. Embora tenham baixo custo individual, aparecem em grande quantidade nos equipamentos eletrônicos. “Para quem investe em empresas ligadas à inteligência artificial, acompanhar esses componentes ajuda a entender riscos que podem não estar refletidos imediatamente nos resultados ou nas expectativas para o setor”, afirma Flávio Vegas, especialista de Produtos da Global X ETFs Brasil. Segundo ele, uma restrição em uma etapa menos conhecida da cadeia pode afetar o ritmo de expansão de empresas ligadas a chips, computação em nuvem e data centers. Servidores de IA ampliam consumo de capacitores O avanço dos servidores de inteligência artificial aumentou de forma significativa o consumo de energia e, consequentemente, a necessidade de componentes capazes de estabilizar o sistema. Um rack Nvidia GB300 NVL72, por exemplo, consome cerca de 142 quilowatts, aproximadamente 16 vezes mais do que um rack de servidor convencional, segundo dados do Uptime Institute reunidos no relatório. Além disso, as placas de computação para IA enfrentam variações de carga milhares de vezes por segundo. Como a fonte de alimentação principal não consegue responder na mesma velocidade, os fabricantes instalam grandes conjuntos de MLCCs próximos aos chips. Com isso, a quantidade de capacitores por equipamento cresce rapidamente. Uma placa de computação tradicional utiliza cerca de 2.500 unidades. Na arquitetura Nvidia GB200, esse número sobe para aproximadamente 6.500. Já na arquitetura Vera Rubin, pode chegar a 12 mil, segundo estimativas da consultoria Aetrix. Quando se considera todo o sistema, incluindo placas de rede, armazenamento, refrigeração e distribuição de energia, um rack GB200 NVL72 pode reunir entre 300 mil e 400 mil MLCCs. Nas próximas gerações, esse volume pode alcançar 600 mil unidades. “O mercado passou os últimos anos concentrado na camada mais visível da inteligência artificial, representada pelos processadores. Agora, a discussão começa a avançar para os componentes que permitem que esses sistemas operem de forma estável”, afirma Vegas. Mercado pode superar US$ 30 bilhões até 2030 O relatório estima que o mercado global de MLCCs pode sair de US$ 15 bilhões em 2025 para mais de US$ 30 bilhões em 2030. Ao fim desse período, inteligência artificial e data centers podem representar cerca de 30% das receitas do setor. Embora o mercado tenha valor inferior ao de semicondutores, uma eventual falta de componentes pode afetar equipamentos de alto valor. Dessa forma, a ausência de peças qualificadas pode limitar a produção ou atrasar entregas destinadas aos data centers. Além da inteligência artificial, a eletrificação também aumenta a demanda. Um veículo elétrico pode utilizar entre 20 mil e 30 mil MLCCs em sistemas como bateria, sensores, câmeras, powertrain e unidades de controle eletrônico. A robótica, a automação industrial e a infraestrutura de energia também contribuem para a expansão desse mercado. Segundo projeção da Mirae Asset Securities, a restrição de MLCCs começa a aparecer como risco emergente em 2026 e pode atingir nível elevado a partir de 2027. Cinco fabricantes concentram mais de 85% da oferta Outro fator de atenção está na concentração da produção. Cinco empresas dominam mais de 85% da oferta global: Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo e TDK. Dados do Morgan Stanley apontam que a Murata detém 41% do mercado. Já a Samsung Electro-Mechanics responde por 23%. Além disso, o processo de fabricação dificulta uma expansão rápida da oferta. Um único capacitor pode reunir entre 500 e mil camadas alternadas de cerâmica e eletrodos metálicos. As fabricantes imprimem, empilham e submetem essas estruturas a temperaturas superiores a mil graus Celsius. Com a redução do tamanho e o aumento da densidade, o controle da produção se torna ainda mais complexo. Novas linhas de fabricação também levam cerca de dois anos para entrar em operação. “O MLCC representa uma fração pequena do custo de um sistema de IA, mas possui uma base de fornecedores concentrada e uma capacidade produtiva que não se expande no mesmo ritmo da demanda”, afirma Vegas. Prazos de entrega chegam a 20 semanas Os servidores de inteligência artificial exigem MLCCs com maior capacidade, tamanho reduzido e resistência térmica de pelo menos 105 graus Celsius durante a operação. Nesse segmento, os prazos de entrega subiram de cerca de oito para até 20 semanas, segundo levantamento da TrendForce. Ao mesmo tempo, o indicador book-to-bill de Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics e Taiyo Yuden atingiu o maior nível desde a pandemia. O índice compara os novos pedidos com os produtos faturados. artigo.texto: VIDEO — How to Stop Data Centers in Your Backyard and Beyond Published Sep 30, 2026 Hear from experts and organizers on the ground on our winning efforts to stop Big Tech’s AI data centers from invading our communities. Fran Caracappa wasn’t expecting to join a campaign against a data center in her small New York town of East Fishkill. “How I came to this fight was by chance,” she said. She was looking at a report from the New York grid operator and found a proposal for a whopping 1GW data center facility in an area of her town near a childcare center and a house of worship. Fran and her neighbors immediately jumped into action to stop this energy-hungry, water-guzzling facility. After months of organizing with Food & Water Watch and other allies, the people of East Fishkill won an incredible victory: a three-year moratorium, or freeze, on new data centers. East Fishkill’s story is echoing in communities across the country. People are unearthing data center deals, organizing with their neighbors, and successfully standing up to Big Tech. At our September Livable Future LIVE, we sat down with Fran and Food & Water Watch experts to learn how you can take on a data center in your backyard and beyond. Watch the Full Event Below! What you’ll learn from “How to Stop Data Centers in Your Backyard and Beyond” (click to expand) Hear from Ben Murray, Food & Water Watch Senior Researcher, Eric Weltman, Food & Water Watch New York Senior Strategist and Organizer, and Fran Caracappa of East Fishkill on: - What data centers are and how they threaten our environment and economy; - How we won a data center moratorium in New York and what we need next; - Six principles to guide your fight against a data center; - What information you need about the planning process and local decision-makers to successfully stop a data center; - How to communicate about data centers to bring more neighbors into the fight; - How to find out if there’s a data center planned for your community; - The myth of data centers as “economic development”; - What closed-looped cooling is and why it won’t solve data centers’ water problems; - And more! artigo.texto: Mercado de carbono abre espaço para o agro regenerativo A transição, porém, exige investimentos iniciais O mercado de créditos de carbono no solo pode se tornar uma fonte adicional de financiamento para a expansão da agricultura regenerativa no Brasil. A combinação entre o potencial agrícola do país, a disponibilidade de áreas para recuperação e a busca por sistemas produtivos de baixo carbono abre espaço para remunerar produtores pela adoção de práticas que aumentem o estoque de carbono e melhorem a qualidade do solo. Análise do Rabobank aponta que o Brasil reúne condições para se tornar um dos principais mercados de créditos de carbono no solo do mundo. Dados da Embrapa citados pelo banco mostram que, dos 177 milhões de hectares de pastagens existentes no país, cerca de 28 milhões de hectares, equivalentes a 15% do total, apresentam algum nível de degradação e poderiam ser restaurados com práticas regenerativas. A transição, porém, exige investimentos iniciais, mudanças no manejo e um período de adaptação. Entre os benefícios associados à agricultura regenerativa estão o aumento da matéria orgânica do solo, ganhos de produtividade, maior retenção de água e redução dos riscos relacionados ao clima. Nesse cenário, o Rabobank avalia que será necessário ampliar os mecanismos de financiamento e remuneração ambiental. Entre as alternativas estão prêmios em cadeias de suprimento sustentáveis, linhas de crédito com condições preferenciais e pagamentos por serviços ambientais, incluindo os créditos de carbono. O mercado já conta com metodologias para medir e monitorar o aumento do carbono armazenado no solo. No Brasil, os primeiros projetos avançam pelas etapas de validação, monitoramento e emissão de créditos. Segundo a análise elaborada por Andrés Padilla, Fernanda Casagrande e Roberto Strumpf, do Rabobank, a expansão dependerá do avanço dos projetos, da adesão dos produtores, do crescimento da demanda, da segurança regulatória e da manutenção da integridade ambiental.

artigo.texto: Jacobs to deploy data center digital twin for NVIDIA’s R&D facility DALLAS – Jacobs (NYSE: J) has been selected by NVIDIA to deploy its Data Center Digital Twin for a large-scale R&D facility in the United States. Under a three-year software-as-a-service agreement, Jacobs will deploy a digital twin environment to enhance operational planning and improve facility performance across one of NVIDIA's most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) research and development facilities. Built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, Jacobs' Data Center Digital Twin creates a real-time environment that helps operators simulate scenarios, while monitoring and optimizing facility performance. The platform integrates engineering models, operational technology and live facility data into a single operational platform, giving operators greater visibility into infrastructure performance. Jacobs Executive Vice President Amer Battikhi said: “As digital infrastructure rapidly scales, operators need smarter and more connected ways to optimize performance and manage energy demand, while improving resiliency. Jacobs is integrating real-time data and simulation technologies to help NVIDIA advance the next generation of AI infrastructure management. The project reflects the growing role of digital twins in helping operators manage critical infrastructure environments.” The digital twin solution will support predictive and simulation-driven use cases including dynamic power load balancing, energy forecasting, liquid coolant leak detection monitoring, predictive maintenance and operator training. Teams can model changing AI workloads to better understand power availability and cooling performance. Beyond visualization and simulation, Jacobs is evolving the digital twin into an intelligent operating system for AI factories, where AI agents continuously learn from facility data to predict conditions, recommend actions and optimize operations with increasing autonomy. The award builds on Jacobs’ work with NVIDIA advancing digital twin technology for AI infrastructure and advanced data center environments. Jacobs is also delivering high-performance computing environments for organizations including Hut 8 in the U.S., SINES DC Campus by Start Campus in Portugal and PsiQuantum in Australia. At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow – delivering outcomes and solutions for the world’s most complex challenges. With approximately $12 billion in annual revenue and a talent force of approximately 47,000, we provide end-to-end services in advanced manufacturing, cities & places, energy, environmental, life sciences, transportation and water. From advisory and consulting, feasibility, planning, design, program and lifecycle management, we’re creating a more connected and sustainable world. artigo.texto: Sometimes, spotting a distinction between opposing political candidates is a challenge, especially on a hot-button issue. But not where data centers are concerned in the race for House District 52, where a longtime local official paints a vastly different picture than his young opponent. In an WW endorsement interview earlier this week, Republican Scott Hege defended the district’s five Google data centers, the first of which he helped land in the mid-aughts as executive director of the Port of The Dalles. “The bottom line is, from my standpoint, everything has been good,” says Hege, who’s served as a Wasco County commissioner for 16 years. “If you look, counties in Oregon are basically all struggling. There are 36 counties, and I bet that there’s not six that are actually in the black. And Wasco County is one of them and, by far, as good as any county in the state.” Data centers have emerged as the issue of the 2026 election. Polling finds an increasing number of Americans feel negatively about them on multiple fronts—the environment, home energy costs, quality of life, local jobs and taxes. Oregon has more than 120 data centers, with several dozen in development—concentrated in several clusters and split by the Cascade Mountains. In total, they receive around $450 million in property tax breaks from various governments. The state has paused new data center development through next summer, with lawmakers eagerly awaiting the recommendations of a governor’s advisory group, due by the end of the year. Hege’s opponent, Hank Sanders, representing the Democratic Party and the Independent Party of Oregon, said knocking on thousands of doors in the district has clued him in to the centrality of the data center issue. Residents complain of rising water rates, an ever-present hum, a lingering “fog” and other problems, he says. “They see that the leaders of these companies aren’t just promising, they’re bragging about how AI is going to replace all of our jobs,” he says. “And we don’t have a vision for how we protect our community from the effects of AI.” Sanders, 25, grew up in Gaston, the son of ZoomCare co-founder Dr. Dave Reynolds and state Sen. Lisa Reynolds (D-West Portland). He spent just a couple of years in journalism (full disclosure: He hosted WW’s podcast for a year) before pivoting to politics; he worked briefly as a campaign political director for U.S. Rep. Maxine Dexter and then most recently worked for his mom as a legislative aide until he decided to run for office. He’s lived in District 52 for just a little over a year. “You can’t tell our neighbors that the 550 million gallons of water going to a corporation and getting dumped back into the Columbia at different temperatures—I actually don’t know what temperatures. They won’t tell us what temperature.” Hege cuts him off. “You should go talk to the [Northern Wasco County Public Utilities District] director. You should talk to the public works director,” Hege says. “You should get the facts.” Sanders supports a statewide moratorium on new data center construction. “For me, it’s important that we pause, address all these issues, before we build another data center,” Sanders says. But he has not made clear how long he thinks that moratorium should last. Though opposed to statewide data center moratoriums, Hege said he supports local bans so long as they’re supported by local communities—a line favored by the GOP’s gubernatorial nominee, state Sen. Christine Drazan (R-Canby). Hege said in The Dalles, data centers have helped fund infrastructure projects that have strengthened the water and electric grids, and rates have not increased. “This is the thing that’s very frustrating from my standpoint,” Hege says. “If you talk to the community leaders in our community—it’s been very good. There’s been, essentially, almost no negative elements. The city has plenty of water, and what’s happened is that development has put lots of money into the city and that’s allowed them to enhance the water system...and the water rates haven’t gone up—you can look.” District 52 covers a vast area around Mount Hood, including all of downtown The Dalles. The House seat is being vacated by Republican Rep. Jeff Helfrich, who’s running for Oregon Senate. The Hege-Sanders result could be close; Helfrich won by tight margins in 2022 and 2024, and nonaffiliated voters comprise 38% of the district’s electorate.

artigo.texto: Packed into a committee room in Frankfort Thursday, dozens of Kentuckians from every corner of the state gathered to tell lawmakers their concerns about — or in one case, support of — developers hoping to set up massive data centers in their communities. “I'm here to let you know that Kentuckians are watching,” Angela Briggs from Barren County. “I can't remember the last time that an issue brought so many different people together, and they're all watching. They're old and young of every race and background, and they're all watching how you handle this issue.” The issues brought to the fore ranged from frustration at how their public officials have dealt with developers, concerns about the effects of pollution on their health and the environment, and anger at tax breaks and the subsequent inaction of the lawmakers to put their own guardrails around data centers. “For nearly 10 months, ordinary people in Mercer County have had to become researchers, investigators, zoning experts, and utility watchdogs because the systems meant to protect us weren't ready,” said Diane Floyd from Mercer County. “Kentucky was ready to recruit this industry by offering huge tax incentives. Kentucky isn't ready to meaningfully protect communities.” Floyd, one of the many leaders in Mercer County fighting a data center development there, said it should not be considered a local issue and demanded legislative action. “Stop expecting local officials without specialized technical, legal, environmental, or utility expertise to negotiate billion-dollar industrial development deals on equal footing with the wealthiest companies on earth,” Floyd said. Proposals for hyperscale data centers have poured into Kentucky since last year with increasing frequency. Kentucky passed a new law to give significant state tax breaks to lure the development of data centers. At first, the tax breaks applied only to Jefferson County, but lawmakers expanded them across the state in 2025. While some believe data center projects will bring major tax revenue for schools and local governments, they have been met with community members’ fears of water, air and noise pollution, jacked-up electric utility bills and lowered property values. Despite the deluge of data center proposals and accompanying bipartisan pushback, the Republican-controlled General Assembly failed to pass protections. One bill passed the state House, but did not gain traction in the Senate. Since then, some lawmakers have doubled down, saying local communities should maintain full control over data center development. Others have expressed concerns over the tax breaks and called for significant protections. Only one speaker Thursday stood up in support of data centers and in opposition to state-level legislation. Martin Rivers, a retired engineer from Fayette County, said he knew he was likely to stand alone at the Thursday meeting, he believes data centers should be treated like infrastructure, like dams, and need to build out rapidly to allow for artificial intelligence growth. "I cannot believe that there is not existing legislation that cover businesses like this,” Rivers said. “Give it to the experts, to people that are employed 365 days a year rather than part-time legislators who don't get to come and do stuff very often.” Eleven lawmakers attended the listening session — all Democrats, except for GOP Rep. Vanessa Grossl of Georgetown. Rep. Adam Moore, a Democrat from Lexington, was co-sponsor on the legislation proposed this year to offer data center protections and organized the meeting. “I think we need to have actual legislation passed, and honestly, that legislation can largely mirror what the government has put out there in an executive order,” Moore said. “I would oppose any new hyperscale data center developments until we have done that.” Gov. Andy Beshear signed an executive order he said would require data centers to cooperate with their communities and not raise power bills. However, advocates say it's unclear how it can be enforced without legislation to back it up. Moore said he wished more of his Republican colleagues had attended the session, but said he is confident there are members of the GOP supermajority who also want safeguards in place. “There's people in leadership positions who are willing to work and get things done. How far they will come along to where the people of Kentucky are — not even asking — demanding that they come along?” Moore said. “That I don't know, but there is clearly an appetite amongst leadership on the House side of real ratepayer protection.” Shawnte West said she purchased a house two years ago just two miles from the 150-acre hyperscale data center planned for Campground Road in west Louisville. “That's why I said I felt really dumb because just two years ago I had no idea that there was a hyperscale data center being placed where I was purchasing a home,” West said. She questioned why data centers should be given large tax breaks — which the left-leaning Center for Economic Development estimated will cost Kentucky more than $1 billion in tax revenue — when many Kentuckians are struggling with healthcare costs and food insecurity. “The state is having to take on millions more dollars to administer the SNAP program, and we're at risk of losing the SNAP program,” West said. “Yet we will give billions of dollars to developers while we can't even feed Kentuckians.” Many speakers also noted extreme concerns about the unfettered growth of artificial intelligence, the surveillance systems they power and lack of federal oversight of AI. “They want us to sacrifice our way of life so they can train AI to replace human workers and collect our data,” said Christie Compton from Breckinridge County. “They want to destroy our communities for profit, and they just expect us to sit back and take it. Well, I say our land is worth more than their data, and we, the people of this commonwealth, have the right to vote no on data centers.”

artigo.texto: American Battery Technology Co (NASDAQ:ABAT) shares rose 10% in premarket trading on Thursday after the company received US government approval to export up to $100 million of recycled black mass material. The approval from the US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security allows American Battery Technology to sell its recycled black mass under specified terms following the introduction of federal export controls covering critical battery materials. Black mass contains materials including lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite, which can be processed and returned to supply chains for use in new products. American Battery Technology processes end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap at its commercial-scale recycling facility near Reno, Nevada, which began operations in 2023. Company Expands Battery Recycling Operations The export licence follows American Battery Technology reporting year-on-year revenue growth of more than 400% for fiscal 2026. "We are grateful for this license and continued support from the U.S. government for the sales of our domestic critical mineral products as we scale both our current critical mineral recycling facility and also our second recycling facility supported by $150 million in competitive grants from the U.S. Department of Energy," CEO Ryan Melsert said. The company is expanding its recycling operations through a second facility supported by $150 million in competitive grants from the US Department of Energy. American Battery Technology said its recycling operations produce copper, aluminium, steel, lithium-rich intermediates and black mass from battery materials using technologies developed internally by the company. artigo.texto: Lemmo prepares e-bike with semi-solid-state battery — The Verge German e-bike manufacturer Lemmo is preparing to launch the Lemmo 3 cargo model — one of the first e-bikes with a semi-solid-state battery. The 960Wh battery is expected to provide a range of up to 180 km, The Verge reports. Battery and powertrain The semi-solid-state electrolyte has a gel-like structure. According to the publication, this technology reduces the risk of thermal runaway compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries and remains stable even if the battery is punctured. Lemmo claims that its battery is 20% more compact and lighter, while its service life is 30% longer. The removable battery can also be used as a power source for AC appliances with output of up to 1,000W and for USB-C devices with output of up to 66W. The bicycle weighs 39 kg with the battery installed, of which the battery accounts for 5 kg. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram. Load capacity and equipment The Lemmo 3 has full suspension, a 24-inch front wheel and a 20-inch rear wheel. The total permitted load is stated at 200 kg: up to 80 kg can be carried on the rear rack and up to 20 kg on the front rack. The model is compatible with MIK HD standard accessories, including child seats, bags and boxes. The rear hub electric motor will have an output of 750W in the United States, 500W in Canada and 250W in Europe. Maximum torque is 90Nm. The company also announced a system that analyzes sensor data and automatically selects a gear. Other equipment includes integrated headlights, turn indicators, brake lights, rear radar, GPS/LTE tracking, a touchscreen display and hydraulic brakes. Price and deliveries A teaser page on Kickstarter has already been opened for EU countries, the United Kingdom, the United States and Canada. Reservations are available with a refundable €39.90 deposit; this makes it possible to purchase the bicycle starting from €1,890 before taxes. Lemmo expects the retail price to exceed €3,390 and plans the first deliveries for April 2027.

artigo.texto: Senate blocks bill aimed at keeping data center costs off electric bills A Senate bill aimed at addressing higher electric costs tied to expanding data centers failed to advance, with Democrats arguing it did not go far enough. The Senate failed to advance a bill on Wednesday aimed at addressing higher electric bills as data centers expand across the country, falling three votes short despite bipartisan agreement on its goal. The vote was 57-43, short of the 60 votes needed to move forward. The measure had previously passed the House 417-3. Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, said, "This bill is the only path that we can take today that will lower electricity prices." Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act, arguing it did not adequately address the issue. Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., said, "Let me be clear, this is nothing more than a messaging bill on the eve of an election." The bill would have required state utility regulators to consider making large power users, such as data centers, pay for the grid upgrades needed to serve them. However, it would not have mandated states to adopt that standard. Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said, "Senate Democrats want to make it mandatory for data centers to cover their own costs by law." Democrats have backed competing proposals that would go further. Heinrich's GRID Savings Act would direct federal regulators to require large electricity customers such as data centers to pay for infrastructure needed to connect them to the grid. Rep. Mike Johnson, R-La., said the Ratepayer Protection Act was "a codification of President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge." The debate over data centers is growing beyond Washington, as communities across the country weigh the promise of new investment against concerns over electric bills and environmental impact. A recent AP-NORC/University of Chicago poll found about 6 in 10 Americans support limiting the number of new data centers, while 63% are concerned about their impact on electricity prices. Taylor Enterline, a Pennsylvania resident, said during a recent community meeting, "We really need strict regulations in place to protect ourselves from data centers." Trump has previously said communities that reject data centers risk "being backwards and poor." When asked about local concerns, Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said, "Nobody has to allow a data center in their hometown if they don't want. I mean, the people of the town will decide. But you know, I think that the places that have allowed data centers in voluntarily have seen the data centers produce more power than they consume, electricity prices have gone down." New economic data released Wednesday shows investment in AI infrastructure, such as data centers, is helping power economic growth. With the bill's failure, Congress has not imposed any new federal protections on data-center-related grid costs. Much of the responsibility remains with states, utility regulators and the agreements that communities strike with companies. The White House has its Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which participating tech companies have voluntarily agreed to cover new power and grid costs their data centers create rather than passing those costs on to existing customers. Husted's legislation was designed to codify key elements of that pledge. Tech companies have been making significant deals with local communities to build data centers. Meta says teachers in Louisiana's Richland Parish received annual bonuses of up to $50,000 because of increased tax revenue associated with its data center project. And on Tuesday, Amazon Web Services agreed to contribute $10 million toward a new career and technical education school in King George County, Virginia, as part of a planned $6 billion data center investment. Trump said Tuesday that people living near data centers could eventually see what he called a "dividend." The question remains whether those benefits outweigh concerns over power costs, water use and the impact on local communities.

artigo.texto: Empresas adotam rotas diferentes para reduzir emissões enquanto SBCE avança Brado Logística, Algar, Tintas Verginia e Vinícola Aurora seguem rotas diferentes; transporte rodoviário, ferroviário e aquaviário só devem entrar no SBCE a partir de 2031, segundo proposta preliminar da Fazenda A descarbonização deixou de ser promessa distante nas decisões das empresas brasileiras, e a regulação ajuda a explicar o movimento. A Lei nº 15.042/2024 criou o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa (SBCE), hoje em fase de regulamentação. Não há, porém, uma rota única: eficiência energética, energia renovável, substituição de combustíveis, gestão de resíduos, mudanças na logística e compensação aparecem em combinações diferentes, conforme o setor e o estágio de cada negócio. A regulação dá o compasso A lei foi publicada em dezembro de 2024 e prevê implementação em cinco fases. A primeira, de regulamentação, dura 12 meses prorrogáveis por mais 12, e o governo trabalha para publicar as normas infralegais até dezembro de 2026. O SBCE adota o modelo cap-and-trade, com cotas brasileiras de emissões (CBEs) e certificados de redução ou remoção verificada (CRVEs), e conviverá com o mercado voluntário de carbono. Quais créditos e metodologias serão aceitos na conciliação ainda será definido. Em 19 de maio, a Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, do Ministério da Fazenda, apresentou proposta preliminar de cobertura setorial em três etapas de quatro anos cada. A primeira, a partir de 2027, abrange papel e celulose, ferro e aço, cimento, alumínio primário, exploração e produção de petróleo e gás, refino e transporte aéreo. A segunda, em 2029, inclui mineração, setor elétrico, vidro, alimentos e bebidas, química, cerâmica e resíduos. A terceira, em 2031, traz os transportes rodoviário, aquaviário e ferroviário. No início, a obrigação é só de relato, sem custo imediato nem meta de redução, e o primeiro Plano Nacional de Alocação deve distribuir cotas gratuitamente. A proposta passou por consulta pública, e a versão final está prevista para este ano. Os caminhos mais usados Os casos do release Brado Logística. A empresa compensou integralmente suas emissões diretas e indiretas: neutralizou 2.822 toneladas com créditos da Usina Hidrelétrica Jirau (RO), usou energia certificada por I-RECs e plantou 280 mudas de Mata Atlântica. Também incorporou caminhões a GNL, que, segundo a companhia, emitem cerca de 25% menos CO₂ e até 90% menos óxidos de nitrogênio que o diesel. A diretora de ESG, Camila Matte, destaca o papel da logística na agenda. “A logística ocupa uma posição estratégica na agenda da descarbonização porque conecta diferentes cadeias produtivas.” Algar. O inventário aponta queda de 44,8% nas emissões totais entre 2021 e 2025. Em 2025, o negócio de TI e telecom compensou 2.304 tCO₂e e a holding, 42 tCO₂e, com créditos de Jirau, projeto verificado pela ONU. Tintas Verginia. Combina eficiência energética, redução de resíduos, melhorias logísticas, certificação Aterro Zero e a condição de Empresa B. Para 2025 e 2026, assumiu o compromisso de medir e compensar emissões estimadas em 1.095 tCO₂e, também com créditos de Jirau, e contribuirá para o plantio de 137 mudas nativas pelo programa Cashback Ambiental. Vinícola Aurora. Mediu 2.454,64 tCO₂e (escopos 1 e 2) em 2025 e, em 2026, prevê compensar integralmente cerca de 2.725 tCO₂e, ainda a validar, com créditos certificados pela Verra, da Usina Hidrelétrica Foz do Chapecó. O Selo Carbon Free® vai aos rótulos. Todas as quatro trabalham com a Carbon Free Brasil, fundada em 2019, que estima chegar a cerca de 200 mil tCO₂e compensadas até o fim de 2026. No porto, a rota é eletrificar Em Santos, a rota mais visível é a troca de equipamentos. A DP World opera com 22 RTGs totalmente elétricos, estima evitar 4.250 toneladas de CO₂ por ano quando 15 novos RTGs entrarem em operação e informa consumo de diesel 29,2% abaixo da média de 2024 entre janeiro e abril deste ano. A Santos Brasil começou a trocar RTGs a diesel por elétricos em 2023, com meta de reduzir em 97% as emissões desses equipamentos. Análise Portogente O ponto central do release é que a compensação aparece como o último degrau de uma escada que começa na medição. Isso é coerente com o que o SBCE sinaliza: nos primeiros anos, o que a regulação cobra é dado confiável (inventário, plano de monitoramento, verificação), e as empresas que já têm essa base saem na frente quando o relato virar obrigação. Há ressalvas. Os volumes citados no release estão na casa de poucos milhares de tCO₂e, abaixo do corte de 10 mil que a lei usa para exigir relato, embora o critério legal valha por fonte ou instalação e não por empresa. Para o setor de transportes, o relógio é mais lento (2031 na proposta preliminar), mas a pressão de grandes clientes e de cadeias de suprimento sobre dados de escopo 3 tende a chegar antes da lei. O que ainda não está claro é como terminais e operações portuárias serão enquadrados dentro de “transporte aquaviário”, e esse é um ponto a acompanhar na versão final.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. FAW Group, GAIG Automobile Form Alliance FAW Group and Guangzhou Automobile Industry Group ("GAIG Automobile"), the controlling shareholder of GAC Group, signed a strategic cooperation framework agreement on September 29. The two state-owned automakers plan to strengthen coordination in assets and capital, technological innovation, and cross-regional industrial resources, drawing on their respective strengths in manufacturing, brands, global operations, and key automotive technologies. The agreement comes as GAC Group advances a major asset restructuring. Under a proposal disclosed on September 28, the listed automaker plans to acquire a 50% stake in FAW Toyota through a share issuance. The strategic partnership and the proposed transaction will move forward in parallel. China Unveils 2026-2030 Battery Plan China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and six other government departments have jointly released a plan for the new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), setting out development goals and key priorities. A key target is to achieve initial large-scale commercialization of all-solid-state batteries by 2030. The plan also calls for major advances in next-generation battery technologies, while targeting a cycle life of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries and product defect rates at the parts-per-billion level for leading manufacturers. The plan outlines 19 key tasks across five areas, including breakthroughs in all-solid-state battery industrialization, development of next-generation battery chemistries and a supply system centered on lithium-ion batteries alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries. It also calls for stronger battery recycling and the development of standards for emerging technologies. Beyond technology, China plans to promote the digital and green transformation of battery manufacturing and support battery companies expanding overseas. The policy also calls for international cooperation and measures to address overseas technical trade barriers, signaling an effort to strengthen China's battery industry across both technology development and global markets. XPeng's Carbon Credit Revenue Tops RMB 1 Billion XPeng has reportedly reached carbon credit deals with Porsche and several other international automakers covering emissions regulations in the EU, UK and Australia, generating more than RMB 1 billion ($140 million) in total revenue. XPeng's vice president confirmed that the reports were accurate, with the company expected to generate more than RMB 500 million in carbon credit revenue in 2026. The deals come as automakers face increasingly stringent emissions requirements in overseas markets. According to European Commission documents, Porsche has opted out of Volkswagen Group's internal CO₂ emissions pool and plans to form an independent open compliance pool for 2026–2027, with XPeng identified as a key partner. Under EU rules, automakers can form emissions pools and use surplus credits from low-emission manufacturers to offset excess emissions. XPeng's growing overseas sales are helping build its position as a potential carbon credit supplier. Its overseas deliveries topped 20,000 units in the second quarter, up 81% year on year, while overseas business accounted for more than 25% of revenue in the first half. From January to July, XPeng ranked first among Chinese new-energy brands in pure-electric sales in several European markets, including Norway, Denmark, France and Portugal. The development highlights a potential new revenue stream for Chinese automakers expanding overseas. As emissions regulations tighten globally, carbon credits are becoming an increasingly strategic asset, allowing automakers with strong EV sales to monetize their regulatory compliance advantages beyond vehicle sales themselves.

artigo.texto: Marisa Wanzeller, da Agência iNFRA A Echoenergia, braço de geração renovável do grupo Equatorial, defende que o leilão de baterias, agendado para dezembro deste ano, seja adiado caso a regra de custeio não mude. Atualmente, a legislação atribui aos geradores o pagamento dos encargos de contratação dos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. “A gente entende que um adiamento de dois a quatro meses, se necessário, é pouco relevante para efeitos do sistema elétrico e é um tempo suficiente para que a gente discuta e resolva o problema”, apontou o CEO da companhia, Liu Aquino, em entrevista à Agência iNFRA. Ele minimizou o risco de uma possível mudança de rota na política energética em 2027: “ninguém vai ser contra uma solução de menor custo marginal para o consumidor”. O executivo afirmou que o modelo vigente gera insegurança jurídica e levará a um leilão pouco competitivo, com custos altos de contratação devido aos riscos. Isso, na sua avaliação, prejudicaria a expansão das baterias no país. Medida Provisória Mesmo que o tema ainda passe por regulamentação na ANEEL (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica), a agência não poderá ultrapassar o dispositivo legal nos seus normativos. Dessa forma, torna-se necessária uma alteração da lei, aponta o CEO da Echoenergia. Para evitar que o certame seja postergado, ele sugere que o governo edite uma MP (Medida Provisória), diante da improbabilidade de o Congresso votar um projeto de lei antes de dezembro. Para ele, apesar da incerteza sobre a aprovação da medida e de sua transformação em lei posteriormente, realizar o leilão durante a vigência da MP daria mais segurança para o investidor do que o cenário atual. “O ideal era que houvesse um projeto de lei aprovado no Congresso. Agora, entre o cenário atual, que não tem nada, e o cenário de ter uma MP que vai ser discutida junto ao legislativo, a gente entende que o cenário da MP é de menor risco.” O deputado federal Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP) apresentou, ainda em julho, o PL (Projeto de Lei) 3.716/2026, que revoga o trecho da Lei 15.269/2025 que é considerado ruim pelos geradores. A matéria, contudo, ainda está parada e – em meio às eleições – tem poucas chances de tramitar nas duas casas legislativas a tempo da realização do certame. Custos O CEO da Echoenergia entende que os geradores vão subsidiar o leilão de baterias, uma vez que o benefício financeiro a eles será menor que o custo dos sistemas de armazenamento. Segundo levantamento da empresa, caso a alternativa de rateio entre todos os geradores conforme a flexibilidade da fonte prevaleça, o custo da contratação para os agentes eólicos e solares ficará em cerca de R$ 10,8 por MWh (megawatt-hora) a cada 5 GW (gigawatts) de potência. Considerando que toda a potência contratada seja utilizada para evitar curtailment, o benefício seria de R$ 2,6/MWh e R$ 4,7/MWh para os geradores eólicos e solares, respectivamente. “O leilão de bateria não está com propósito ou com racional econômico de atender os geradores e eles estariam pagando por isso. Na prática, o leilão de bateria estaria sendo subsidiado por investimentos que já foram feitos, por contratos e outorgas que estão no sistema há alguns anos e estariam pagando esta compra”, avalia Liu Aquino. Dessa forma, o executivo entende que a contratação deve ser bancada pelo consumidor, uma vez que o principal objetivo do leilão seria atender à demanda nos horários de “ponta”, quando a carga aumenta e a geração renovável cai. Na visão do CEO, a contratação dos sistemas de armazenamento irá reduzir a necessidade de contratação de térmicas, levando a um benefício econômico. Enquanto as baterias custariam entre R$ 600/MWh e R$ 800/MWh, as termelétricas seriam cerca de R$ 2.300/MWh. Acesso à transmissão Outro ponto que preocupa os agentes, segundo Liu Aquino, é a falta de regulamentação da Pnast (Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão) antes da realização do leilão de baterias. Isso porque, sem uma especificação, os sistemas de armazenamento terão que concorrer por espaço na rede durante as temporadas de acesso. O ideal, do ponto de vista da Echoenergia, seria o espaço na rede garantido para os lotes que ganharem o certame. “Esse processo de aprovação de conexão do sistema de bateria precisa ser sujeito somente a questões técnicas, e não a fluxo de potência. A restrição do fluxo de potência já tem que ser definida no leilão, porque não dá para o empreendedor entrar lá no leilão e assumir todos os compromissos para ver se vai poder conectar depois”, apontou.

artigo.texto: Candidates in 5th Congressional District race discuss AI and data centers at forum Republican and Democratic candidates weigh in on energy production and environmental concerns MONROE, La. (KNOE) - A forum was held Tuesday night for the 5th Congressional District race, featuring candidates from both major parties. Republican candidates Stewart Cathey, Misti Cordell, Michael Echols, Gabe Firment and Austin Magee attended the forum. On the Democratic side, Dan McKay and Pat Moore also weighed in. One topic at the forefront of the forum was artificial intelligence and data centers. When asked about energy production and environmental concerns surrounding the growing industry, Republican candidates Magee, Firment and Cathey said there needs to be some oversight. “What frustrates me is seeing that all of this red tape being cut for AI companies when the people need more power, we need better infrastructure, we can’t seem to get it. But the second that a small group of elites want to build God in a box and build these massive AI data centers, all red tape is immediately cut for them and they can have whatever they want,” Magee said. “The first thing that Congress needs to do is pass Ratepayer Protection Act which will ensure that as we see this growth of energy resources being spent here in this country that the companies that are actually using the energy are the ones that are paying it, not passing it on to the rate payer,” Cathey said. “You have to protect the consumer. It’s also absolutely imperative that we take care of our water and our natural resources. I passed House Resolution 374 last session to instruct the state to do just that, to study the use of one of our most precious natural resources, our water,” Firment said. Two Republicans, Cordell and Echols, said they see the lack of infrastructure for data centers as an opportunity to grow. “Nuclear is something that’s very effective and it’s also clean. Also hardening our grids. That’s something we have not done since the 70s. And the pellet technology. Part of this district is loggers, so any of the pellet technology could be a new version of energy,” Cordell said. “I passed a resolution that would encourage more nuclear, small nuclear reactor, and other types of fuels. I think Louisiana is a fuel-rich state. We just have to use the resources we’ve got to produce that,” Echols said. The Democratic candidates agreed with Magee, Cathey and Firment, saying there needs to be more regulations and laws placed on this type of growth. “I just believe that they have a lot of constitutional power. We’re going to have to look to make sure that we exercise that. And anything that is not healthy, not for the best interests of the people, then they’re going to have to make that decision,” Moore said. “We need some rules. And I say we get together in Congress and we make some rules to control the haphazard growth of these types of things,” McKay said. Republican Oscar “Omar” Dantzler and Democrat Antonio Wilson were not in attendance. The deadline to register to vote in the November election is Oct. 5, by mail or in person. If you would like to register to vote, you can visit the Secretary of State’s website here. The full forum can be found on under the streaming tab of our website. Copyright 2026 KNOE. artigo.texto: Addressing more than 20 global corporate executives at the High-Level and CEO Forum on Low-Emission Rice and Sustainable Agriculture in New York, the minister emphasized that carbon pricing mechanisms would allow investors to unlock additional financial value from verifiable emissions reductions in Indonesia. "Indonesia is facing a waste emergency that must be addressed immediately, one of which is through waste-to-energy. Therefore, the government is encouraging green investment in the waste sector as a priority," Zulkifli said in a statement on Tuesday (September 29). Zulkifli outlined three primary sectors open to green investment: sustainable agriculture through low-emission rice cultivation, waste-to-energy processing, and marine conservation through blue carbon development. As chair of the Carbon Economic Value (NEK) Steering Committee, he said Jakarta is streamlining regulatory frameworks and strengthening carbon trading governance to ensure high-credibility carbon assets. A key step came on July 6, 2026, when the Financial Services Authority (OJK) enacted POJK No. 10/2026, mandating that all exchange-traded carbon units be formally registered under the Carbon Unit Registry System (SRUK). OJK data as of August 31, 2026, revealed that 159 service users have registered on the Indonesian Carbon Exchange since its inception on September 26, 2023. Total transaction volume reached 1.98 million tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), with a cumulative value of Rp93.90 billion (approximately US$5.24 million). Government projections indicate that the carbon pricing framework could mobilize up to US$5.80 billion in green investment while reducing greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 570 million tCO2e. Beyond waste management, Indonesia is seeking various international partners to scale up low-emission rice production to strengthen domestic food security while reducing agricultural methane emissions. Zulkifli noted that implementing low-emission rice cultivation on a large scale requires technological support, financing, market certainty, and clear economic benefits for farmers. He added that climate action must translate into concrete, field-level projects that directly benefit farmers and coastal communities. artigo.texto: A margem de conexão disponível no Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) para os leilões de baterias de dezembro é estimada em cerca de 56 GW, segundo cálculo da Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae) a partir de nota técnica do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS). O volume é até 12,5 vezes superior à necessidade de potência estimada para o período de 2028 a 2030, de 4,5 GW a 10 GW, indicando, na avaliação da entidade, que a disponibilidade de rede não deve representar uma restrição generalizada para os projetos que disputarão os certames, previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro. A partir dos limites apresentados para os diferentes pontos da rede, a Absae calculou uma margem de conexão de aproximadamente 56 GW no SIN. Considerando a estimativa de déficit de potência entre 2028 e 2030, de 4,5 GW a 10 GW, a margem disponível equivale a entre 5,6 e 12,5 vezes a necessidade estimada. Nos barramentos bonificados pela portaria nº 136/2026, a margem agregada chega a aproximadamente 13,7 GW. Segundo a associação, esse volume, isoladamente, já supera a estimativa mais alta de déficit de potência. A portaria do Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME) mencionada pela associação é a que estabelece as diretrizes para os certames. A entidade avalia que há espaço de conexão distribuído por diferentes regiões do sistema para receber projetos de armazenamento, reduzindo o risco de uma restrição generalizada de rede para os empreendimentos que disputarão os leilões. “A nota do ONS é uma boa notícia para o leilão. A rede tem margem de cerca de 56 GW, bem acima da necessidade de potência que estimamos para os próximos anos, e esse espaço está distribuído por várias regiões, mantendo a competitividade de grande parte dos projetos cadastrados. O atendimento ao cronograma também é salutar e mostra o compromisso da governança do setor elétrico em cumprir os prazos do leilão. Com tantos projetos cadastrados, a disputa deve ser decidida por preço, o que favorece o consumidor”, afirma Fabio Lima, diretor-executivo da ABSAE. Margem identificada em pontos bonificados e não bonificados Dos 129 barramentos bonificados, 93 têm margem reconhecida. Eles se concentram no Nordeste, sobretudo na Bahia, no Piauí e no Ceará, e no norte de Minas Gerais, regiões que reúnem os maiores blocos de capacidade, de até cerca de 3,7 GW. Em outros pontos, a margem é menor ou compartilhada entre vários barramentos. Também há locais sem margem em razão de restrições de espaço físico, curto-circuito ou cronograma de obras. O desenho dos leilões já prevê esse tipo de ajuste, com classificação por barramento, subárea e área. Nos barramentos definidos como estratégicos pela Portaria nº 136/2026, os projetos contam com uma bonificação de 10% no preço de classificação. O mecanismo busca incentivar a instalação de baterias em pontos da rede onde os sistemas podem oferecer benefícios adicionais ao sistema elétrico. Projetos localizados em outras regiões, que somam cerca de 36 GW de margem, também competem nos leilões, ampliando o espaço disponível para os empreendimentos. A bonificação considera pontos da rede onde, além de potência, os sistemas de armazenamento podem contribuir para aumentar a robustez elétrica, especialmente em locais com menor capacidade de manter a tensão estável. Os sistemas de baterias exigidos nos leilões têm capacidade de operar como formadores de rede e fornecer esse suporte, contribuindo para a estabilidade da rede nesses pontos e reduzindo a necessidade de outras soluções, como compensadores síncronos. Por isso, os projetos conectados a esses barramentos têm o preço de classificação reduzido em 10%, sem perda de receita. Competição deve permanecer elevada A Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) cadastrou 6.091 projetos para os leilões, que somam 296,8 GW. Mesmo com a redução natural decorrente da habilitação técnica e da disponibilidade de rede, a Absae avalia que o número de projetos aptos seguirá muito acima da quantidade a ser contratada. Na avaliação da associação, esse cenário mantém elevada a competição entre os empreendimentos e pode contribuir para uma contratação mais eficiente e para a redução de custos ao consumidor.
