artigo.texto: Volkswagen slows gigafactory battery manufacturing plans in Ontario Subscribe to our free newsletter today to keep up to date with the latest manufacturing news. Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary PowerCo is pushing back the start of operations at its St. Thomas, Ontario, gigafactory to 2029, extending a timetable that had originally targeted the first battery cells for 2027 and giving the company more time to align production with changing market conditions. The shift adds two years to the schedule for one of Canada’s largest electric vehicle manufacturing investments, but it does not represent a retreat from the project because construction is continuing and the planned industrial scale remains largely unchanged. Volkswagen has said the plant could represent an investment of as much as C$7 billion, or about US$4.9 billion, by 2030, with annual production capacity eventually reaching up to 90 GWh and as many as 3000 direct skilled jobs supported at full development, alongside additional employment across the regional supply chain. The revised timetable matters beyond St. Thomas because battery manufacturers are trying to build factories that will operate for decades while the market they are designed to serve is evolving far more quickly, particularly as EV demand, vehicle platforms, battery chemistry and manufacturing economics continue to change. The two-year extension could strengthen the factory’s production ramp St. Thomas holds an important position in PowerCo’s global manufacturing network because Volkswagen has described the Ontario facility as the company’s first overseas gigafactory and its largest planned battery cell factory. At full expansion, the plant’s potential annual capacity of 90 GWh would make it a significant supplier to Volkswagen Group electric vehicle production in North America, giving the company a large regional source of battery cells while reducing dependence on longer and more complex international supply chains. The plant is based on PowerCo’s standardized factory concept and Unified Cell strategy, which are designed to create greater manufacturing consistency across several locations while still allowing battery cells to be adapted to different vehicle requirements and market conditions. Moving the start of operations from 2027 to 2029 changes the economics of the production ramp because a battery factory does not create value simply by having its equipment installed and its production lines available. Its financial performance depends heavily on utilization rates, production yields, material costs, customer demand and the ability to operate complex equipment at a sufficiently high volume to spread fixed costs across a large number of cells. Bringing major production capacity online before vehicle manufacturers are ready to absorb it can create an expensive mismatch between supply and demand, leaving costly machinery operating below its intended utilization rate while manufacturers continue to carry significant fixed operating expenses. A more gradual commissioning schedule gives battery producers more room to align cell output with vehicle programs, supplier contracts and regional demand rather than bringing large volumes online before the market can consistently support them. This approach has become more relevant as automakers reassess the pace of their electric vehicle investments and reconsider how quickly new platforms, factories and battery programs should be introduced across North America. The shift does not suggest that electrification has stopped, but it does show that manufacturers are becoming more selective about when individual factories should reach full production and how quickly capital-intensive capacity should be brought into service. For suppliers, logistics operators and industrial service providers, a two-year change to battery production can affect warehouse planning, inbound material contracts, equipment commissioning, workforce requirements, transport volumes and the timing of supplier investments tied to the plant. PowerCo can use the extra time to transfer technology from Europe The revised schedule could have another important consequence because the St. Thomas factory that begins producing batteries in 2029 may benefit from substantially more manufacturing experience than the plant that was originally expected to begin operations two years earlier. PowerCo began cell production at its Salzgitter gigafactory in Germany in late 2025, and Volkswagen has positioned that facility as the lead plant for subsequent battery operations in Valencia, Spain, and St. Thomas. That structure gives the Canadian operation more time to absorb production knowledge developed elsewhere in the network before it moves into high-volume manufacturing, which could influence how equipment is configured, how quality is managed and how operating procedures are designed. Battery manufacturing is particularly sensitive to this type of learning because improvements in production yield, quality control, energy consumption, material handling and equipment reliability can materially change the cost of every cell leaving a factory. Experience accumulated during the ramp-up of earlier plants can therefore affect the performance of later facilities, particularly when production teams are able to identify recurring problems before new factories reach commercial scale. Battery chemistry is evolving at the same time, creating another reason why a later production date could materially affect how the St. Thomas operation is configured when it begins manufacturing cells. artigo.texto: Alberto Kuba, CEO da WEG: 'não imaginávamos que teria esse boom' (Leandro Fonseca/Exame) Repórter Publicado em 30 de setembro de 2026 às 05h00. A multinacional fabricante de equipamentos elétricos WEG anunciou, entre sexta-feira, 25, e segunda-feira, 28, novos investimentos em baterias e geradores para atender à expansão de data centers e redes elétricas. BTG Pactual, Ativa Investimentos e Citi veem potencial de crescimento nos projetos, embora o impacto sobre os resultados deva ocorrer de forma gradual. A WEG (WEGE3) não esperava o ritmo que os data centers imprimiriam ao negócio de geradores. "Não imaginávamos que teria esse boom", afirmou Alberto Kuba, CEO da companhia, em entrevista para a edição 2026 do prêmio Maiores e Melhores, da Revista EXAME. Segundo o executivo, a demanda pelo equipamento ganhou força com a expansão dos data centers, que precisam de grupos geradores para garantir o fornecimento de energia em caso de interrupções. E a reação da companhia a esse movimento vem aparecendo cada vez mais nos investimentos.Na última sexta-feira, 25, a multinacional que fabrica equipamentos elétricos anunciou a ampliação da fábrica de baterias em Santa Catarina e, três dias depois, na segunda, 28, divulgou um investimento de US$ 165 milhões, cerca de R$ 869 milhões, para aumentar a produção de geradores na América do Norte. Os dois movimentos colocam a WEG em uma frente que combina geração, armazenamento e infraestrutura elétrica — e que ganhou força com o avanço dos data centers e a necessidade de redes mais robustas. Para o BTG Pactual (do mesmo grupo controlador da EXAME), Ativa Investimentos e Citi, os movimentos colocam a WEG em segmentos que podem sustentar o crescimento da companhia nos próximos anos, embora os efeitos dos novos investimentos sobre os resultados devam aparecer de forma gradual. No caso da iniciativa para ampliar a capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte, o projeto será dividido em duas fases e foi anunciado com foco na crescente demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos Estados Unidos, especialmente para atender à expansão dos data centers. A primeira fase receberá US$ 24 milhões para a aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial próximo ao atual Parque Industrial Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e tem início de operação previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda etapa, a WEG pretende investir US$ 141 milhões na construção de duas novas instalações industriais, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte. A estrutura terá produção verticalizada, incluindo a fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças. Com a conclusão da segunda fase, prevista para 2030, a capacidade global da WEG para fabricar geradores deverá passar das atuais 10 unidades por dia para cerca de 50. A produção será distribuída entre as fábricas da companhia no México, EUA, Brasil e China. O movimento amplia uma operação que já vem se beneficiando da expansão dos data centers. "O negócio de alternadores, sob a marca Marathon, tem apresentado um forte desempenho, apoiado pela robusta demanda por energia de reserva por parte dos data centers", escreveu o BTG em relatório nesta terça-feira, 29. Para o banco, o novo investimento aumenta a capacidade da WEG de atender a uma demanda que tende a exigir cada vez mais equipamentos para garantir o fornecimento de energia. O BTG considera o anúncio positivo e afirma que a expansão cria uma plataforma para o crescimento do negócio de geração de energia da companhia na América do Norte no médio prazo. O banco, porém, ressalta que o investimento não deve trazer uma contribuição relevante para o lucro imediatamente. Mas ressalta que "embora os gastos de capital iniciais impliquem uma contribuição limitada para os lucros no curto prazo, a adição de capacidade deve proporcionar uma plataforma para um maior crescimento dos negócios de geração de energia da WEG na América do Norte no médio prazo", afirmou. "A WEG realizará seu Investor Day nesta semana, onde esperamos mais detalhes sobre sua estratégia para aproveitar as oportunidades de crescimento no mercado norte-americano", acrescentou o banco sobre o evento que ocorre nesta sexta-feira, 2. O investimento em geradores veio três dias depois de outro anúncio relacionado à infraestrutura de energia. Na sexta-feira, 25, a WEG ampliou o projeto de sua fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, os BESS, em Itajaí, no litoral norte catarinense. O investimento previsto para a unidade passou de R$ 280 milhões para R$ 330 milhões, enquanto a capacidade anual de produção foi dobrada, de 2 para 4 gigawatts-hora (GWh). O início das operações está previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027. A expansão ocorre às vésperas do primeiro leilão de armazenamento de energia do país, previsto para dezembro de 2026. A expectativa é de crescimento da demanda por baterias para integrar fontes renováveis, como solar e eólica, ao sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Ativa Investimentos, há aí uma oportunidade para a WEG. "Como temos discutido, as iniciativas de BESS e o crescimento de data centers são os principais gatilhos para destravar valor para a companhia", disse o analista da casa, Lucas Dias. O Citi também coloca os dois anúncios dentro de uma mesma tese. Para o banco, geradores para data centers e sistemas de armazenamento aumentam a exposição da WEG a dois segmentos ligados à expansão da infraestrutura energética. No caso dos geradores, o Citi destaca que a capacidade global da companhia deverá passar de 10 para 50 unidades por dia após a conclusão do projeto em 2030. Já no BESS, chama atenção para a velocidade da expansão: em sete meses, a WEG dobrou a capacidade planejada da fábrica e aumentou o investimento em R$ 50 milhões. artigo.texto: Alphabet launched its homegrown AI chips into orbit on Thursday in a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, a step towards making data centers in space a reality. The launch window opened at 11:15 am PT from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California's Santa Barbara County, with liftoff occurring without incident. SpaceX successfully deployed all payloads on board by 1 p.m. local time. SpaceX has promoted supercomputers in space as the next frontier in artificial intelligence infrastructure, touting "infinite real estate" in orbit as a means of escaping the data center backlash on the ground. During the uncrewed Transporter-18 mission, SpaceX will carry Planet Labs satellites, including a solar-powered prototype equipped with Google's tensor processing units (TPUs). The Thursday launch marks the first in-orbit test for Alphabet's Project Suncatcher, a "moonshot" initiative Google first revealed in November 2025. The company aims to develop reliable, solar-powered AI computing infrastructure that can operate continuously in space. "Our team has confirmed contact with the satellite and it is operating as expected," Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher, wrote in a blog post following the launch. He called it the first step in a long-term research effort, "exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure." Alphabet is a significant investor in SpaceX, which went public in June in a record IPO, and the businesses are close partners even as their AI divisions compete with one another. Alphabet's stake in SpaceX is currently valued at over $82 billion. In low Earth orbit, satellites can "access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth," Alphabet said in the post. Eventually, they expect to be able to "link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit." The Google parent has already tested its TPUs running AI workloads in a facility at the University of California at Davis, but doesn't yet know how its chips will perform in the challenging conditions of low Earth orbit. SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, has also announced that it plans to build and launch its own orbital data centers. They will be comprised of swarms of satellites the company develops in Redmond, Washington, equipped with graphics processing units and solar arrays it plans to produce with Tesla, Musk's automaker. Earlier this year, Musk said data centers in space would be the cheapest way to train AI, "and that will be true within two years, maybe three at the latest." SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said at an event in September that the company will deploy "supercompute in space" in 2027. Industry experts say space-based data centers represent a far-out mission, if they can even become feasible, in part because rocket launches remain capacity-constrained and expensive. Orbital data centers would also require cooling systems and chips that can withstand extreme temperatures, as well as protection from radiation. Clutter and orbital debris could also impede their viability. The Transporter-18 flight was the second major launch in a single day for SpaceX, which also began transporting astronauts to the International Space Station from Florida's Space Coast for NASA with an earlier liftoff on Thursday, marking the start of a six-month mission in orbit. artigo.texto: Anju Singh served as the host for a community forum in Cumberland County about data centers on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. Haley O'Brien / WITF Curious and concerned residents heard from experts, officials and organizers about data center development — and efforts to challenge it — during a community forum in Cumberland County on Tuesday. Environmental lawyers discussed the developments’ potential effect on the region’s water and power grid while organizers of local grassroots groups shared tips for residents concerned about proposed projects. John Werner is a member of Stewards of Cumberland County, an advocacy group that formed in response to data center developments. “We were one of the first organizations that formed locally, and we formed because people were not getting off Facebook,” he said. Werner spoke about what he called “the importance of people power.” “There are residents who have mounted robust challenges in municipalities all over the place and beat these data centers,” Werner said. “And our strongest weapon in this fight is one another.” Michael Ewall, founder of the Energy Justice Network, shared how the developments are projected to strain the power grid. “By 2030, we need about 60% increase in electric generation to meet the demand… which is largely being driven by the data center boom,” he said. Residents concerned about potential data center developments in their neighborhoods also asked what they can do to challenge the projects. “I feel very tiny in a very big space,” said Harrisburg resident Amara Nazario, who is in the early stages of forming a community group to advocate against proposed developments in Swatara Twp., Dauphin County. “I’m still just wrapping my head around everything and jumping into a fight,” she said. Werner recommended those who live in a community with a project in the works to find a way to slow down the process. “The more hurdles that you can throw up, the more inconvenient it is for the developers,” he said. Amy Zeigler, from the group Protect South Hanover PA, had flyers and a presentation prepared to show the impact of a proposed data center on surrounding communities. She suggested groups work together and share each other’s strengths, including graphic design, public speaking and organizational skills. Dauphin County Commissioner Justin Douglas did not say he supports data centers. But he said municipalities are struggling to balance budgets and these expensive developments can provide significant revenue. artigo.texto: A receita fixa de 15 anos prevista no Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade (LRCap) de armazenamento não é o único fator considerado pelos players na definição dos lances para a disputa prevista para dezembro. De acordo com a Clean Energy Latin America (Cela), projetos de baterias associados a usinas solares e eólicas também estão incorporando na modelagem ganhos com a redução de cortes de geração, do Montante de Uso do Sistema de Transmissão (Must) e riscos de conexão. A receita definida no leilão é a principal referência para os bancos na avaliação do financiamento dos projetos. No entanto, outros componentes podem alterar de forma significativa a economia dos empreendimentos e, consequentemente, a estratégia adotada por cada participante na formação do lance. Um dos fatores considerados é o chamado curtailment evitado, ou seja, a redução dos cortes de geração proporcionada pela presença da bateria. De acordo com Vinicius Henrique, gerente sênior de Estratégia e Análise de Investimentos da consultoria, quanto mais próximo o BESS estiver de um projeto solar ou eólico existente, maior pode ser o impacto da redução dos cortes sobre a geração da usina associada. Com isso, alguns players avaliam a possibilidade de vincular o projeto de armazenamento a ativos renováveis que já operam, buscando capturar esse valor adicional além da receita do contrato do leilão. Outro componente considerado é o Must. Segundo a Cela, projetos associados podem ter uma redução de até 30% nesse custo. O fator ganha relevância na modelagem porque, para o leilão, não haverá desconto na Tarifa de Uso do Sistema de Transmissão (Tust). “Esse é um aspecto que está puxando bastante, dependendo do quão agressivos os players querem ser nessa tomada de decisão de quanto dá para considerar dessa Tust e desse curtailment para o seu próprio projeto. Então, a gente vê diversos players encarando isso de formas muito diferentes. É o primeiro leilão, muitas novidades e incertezas ainda. A gente não tem muito claro e cada empresa encara isso de uma forma diferente. É muito interessante essas diferentes abordagens para o mesmo projeto e como isso impacta, no fim do dia, o bid para o leilão que vai ser em dezembro”, comentou em painel do Storage Leaders, evento promovido pela Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar) em São Paulo nesta quarta-feira, 30 de setembro. Cinco anos após o contrato Outro ponto que começa a diferenciar as modelagens é o período posterior aos 15 anos de contrato previstos no leilão. Segundo o executivo, as baterias podem operar por cerca de 20 anos, o que abre uma discussão sobre a utilização dos cinco anos adicionais de vida operacional dos equipamentos. A questão é relevante porque, após o término do contrato, a estrutura de custos do projeto muda. A Cela destaca especialmente o peso da Tust, que precisa ser considerada tanto no carregamento quanto no descarregamento da bateria. A consultoria afirma que clientes já discutem se projetos associados ao leilão poderão manter, no período posterior aos 15 anos, eventuais benefícios relacionados à colocalização. A definição desse ponto pode produzir diferenças relevantes entre os projetos na modelagem de retorno. Conexão pode pesar na competitividade A conexão à rede também aparece como um diferencial para projetos associados a usinas que já possuem acesso ao sistema. Vinicius Henrique destacou que os vencedores do leilão terão que passar por uma nova temporada de acesso, conforme a regulamentação vigente, o que adiciona um componente de risco de cronograma para empreendimentos que ainda não possuem conexão. Nesse cenário, associar a bateria a um projeto solar ou eólico que já tenha conexão pode representar uma vantagem não apenas em termos de Capex, mas também de risco. A avaliação é que esses projetos podem apresentar maior competitividade na disputa justamente pela combinação de menor necessidade de investimentos em conexão e menor exposição ao risco associado ao cronograma de acesso. Preço das baterias e augmentation O preço dos equipamentos também permanece como uma variável relevante na preparação dos lances. Ele afirmou que ainda existe incerteza sobre os preços de baterias nacionais e importadas e que a definição das margens para os projetos associados, especialmente no Nordeste, pode influenciar a competição no leilão. Outro ponto destacado pela consultoria é o chamado augmentation, estratégia relacionada à reposição ou expansão da capacidade das baterias ao longo da vida útil do projeto. Segundo o gerente, as curvas de augmentation variam de acordo com fatores como o perfil do cliente, as condições de financiamento, a estratégia operacional e o nível de risco assumido por cada participante. A recomendação apresentada pela consultoria aos players é que essas curvas sejam incorporadas à modelagem financeira, já que o momento e o volume dos investimentos adicionais podem alterar o retorno dos projetos.

artigo.texto: - Colombia’s Environment Ministry plans to revoke Decree 973 of 2026, which established rules for the country’s carbon market. - The government cited procedural issues and plans to develop a replacement framework with broader participation. - Environment Minister Fabio Arjona wants to strengthen the national emissions registry and attract private investment. Colombia’s government is moving to revoke regulations governing its carbon market, reopening a policy framework adopted only weeks ago under former President Gustavo Petro, local news website La Silla Vacía reported Tuesday, citing Environment Minister Fabio Arjona. Arjona announced the decision during Medellín Climate Week, saying the government would begin the process of withdrawing Decree 973 of 2026. The measure was issued shortly before Petro left office and introduced requirements for carbon projects, including emissions verification, community participation and government oversight of international credit sales. The Environment Ministry said its review found that the Finance Ministry had not participated in matters within its remit and that opinions from other government agencies were still pending when the decree was issued. The ministry also said the final text had undergone substantial changes without being republished for public comment. Government Plans Replacement Framework The government says revoking the decree is intended to correct those procedural issues while developing a new regulatory system involving communities, territories, private companies and public agencies. Arjona said the government aims to build a stronger National Registry of Greenhouse Gas Emission Reductions, known as Renare, and establish rules intended to encourage private capital to support conservation and emissions reductions. He said the administration expects to have a new version of Renare ready within three months. Relevant: Former Colombia President Iván Duque Takes Key Role In Global Carbon Accounting Push The decree had also extended potential project durations, allowing some emissions reduction projects to operate for up to 15 years and removal projects for as long as 40 years. Industry representatives nevertheless raised concerns that government approval between project phases could increase costs and deter foreign investment. The ministry said existing rules will remain in effect while the replacement framework is developed. Read more: Amazon Tribes Triumph In Landmark Carbon Credit Lawsuit In Colombia

artigo.texto: Community voices concerns ahead of new AI data center in Jefferson Davis County JEFFERSON DAVIS COUNTY, Miss. (WDAM) - A digital infrastructure campus is coming to Jefferson Davis County. The developer, Eagle Rock Partners, held a public hearing Tuesday evening to address concerns. Some residents worry about water usage, power rates and the amount of noise the campus will cause, while others want to have a say in whether they build it or not. “We’re concerned about how the traffic for them trying to build this is going to affect our daily lives,” Bassfield Resident Patti Warren said. “There’s a lot involved in all of this, and we just think that the community should have a right to be able to vote.” The campus will cover 800 acres of land near Gum Swamp Road and the Covington County line. Eagle Rock Members say it will offer a projected 200 full-time operational jobs and over 1,000 construction jobs. Economic Development Association Executive Director Gary Russell Bass understands the negative feelings surrounding AI data centers, but he wants the public to understand the opportunities this will bring to the county. “I’ve done a lot of research on this company, I’ve done a lot of research on what they’re saying, and I think that the information that they’re trying to provide the community is a step in the right direction,” Bass said. “I just hope that everybody would come with an open mind, and get all of their questions answered.” Ken Lober with Eagle Rock Partners wanted the meeting to leave no box unchecked. With a project like this already in motion, Lober wanted the community to be involved and know the “why” behind the project. “We aspire to be completely transparent, and this is a big step towards that,” Lober said. “To have the community come out, ask any questions they want, walk through the facts of what this project is, then work with the economic development agency, the county supervisors, and to be able to make sure that the county engineer and everybody validate what we’re saying we’re going to do, and that we do it.” This campus is an estimated $6 billion capital investment. Construction for the new campus is set to begin sometime in 2027. Want more WDAM 7 news in your inbox? Click here to subscribe to our newsletter. Copyright 2026 WDAM. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Gotion High-Tech and Inobat are launching a new battery ecosystem in Valladolid, starting with a €940 million investment and plans for 1,000 jobs. This move signals a new phase in Spain’s electric vehicle industry and intensifies competition among global battery giants. Gotion High-Tech is moving into Valladolid. The company has picked this Spanish city for its next European project, putting down €940 million to kick off a new battery ecosystem with Inobat. The first step: a cathode factory and a recycling plant in Palomares. That means 1,000 new jobs. It also shows Spain is becoming more important in the electric vehicle supply chain. This isn’t Gotion’s first big play in Spain. Not long ago, the company bought a 49% stake in the Sagunto gigafactory from Volkswagen’s PowerCo. That deal brought €1.1 billion into a joint venture focused on LFP battery cells and cathode materials. Now, German and Chinese partners share the facility. PowerCo and EFE report that the Sagunto plant will open in early 2027. It will employ 1,500 people and is expected to reach 30 GWh of annual capacity. Gotion’s network already stretches from Šurany in Slovakia to Kenitra in Morocco. The company is building a pan-European battery chain, one step at a time. Spain is now a hotspot for battery makers. Chinese investment leads the way. CATL, the world’s biggest battery producer, has teamed up with Stellantis for a €4.1 billion project near Zaragoza. They want full production by 2028 and plan to hire 4,000 people. Envision is also in the mix. Its LFP battery plant will start with 12.5 GWh capacity and 900 jobs. If the market grows, that could jump to 3,000 workers and 94 GWh. The numbers are huge. Projects from CATL, Envision, and others now total €8.365 billion and nearly 7,500 jobs across Spain. Some projects are smaller but still matter. The Leapmotor-Stellantis joint venture opened a battery workshop in Mallén last year. It invested €25 million and hired 90 people. The plant can make up to 60,000 LFP cells a year. Even these modest efforts add to Spain’s fast-changing industrial scene. The country is turning into a European hub for electrification. Gotion’s Valladolid plan is bold. It’s not just about assembly lines. The company wants to build a full battery ecosystem. That means making anodes, setting up assembly, and opening research and development centers. But the full €5 billion investment depends on how the first phase goes. Gotion and Inobat have both said future growth will hinge on the success of the first facilities. Construction is set to start in 2027. Chinese battery investment in Spain is rising fast. New electric vehicle brands are arriving too. As reported earlier, GAC AION UT has entered the Spanish market, challenging established names with European-built models and sharp pricing. Battery plants and car factories are coming together. The competition is heating up. Spain is now a key battleground for global electrification. The new projects are different. They focus on the whole supply chain, not just assembly. The Valladolid project will make cathodes and recycle materials. This cuts dependence on outside suppliers and gives more control over raw materials. It could give Spain an edge as European carmakers race to lock in battery deals and technology partners. Gotion’s careful expansion, strong partners, and phased investment show a bigger trend. Spain is no longer just a market for electric cars. It’s a main player in the battery race. What happens next depends on execution, demand, and whether these alliances deliver. For now, the facts are clear. Billions in investment. Thousands of jobs. A new industrial map is taking shape in Spain.

artigo.texto: Porto Central pode receber investimento em data centers Porto estuda estrutura para receber data centers, com oferta de energia e conexão por cabos submarinos O Porto Central, em Presidente Kennedy, desenvolve um projeto para implantar um hub de data centers voltado a empresas do Brasil e do exterior. A iniciativa pretende aproveitar a oferta de energia do Espírito Santo e a infraestrutura do complexo portuário para criar uma nova frente de desenvolvimento econômico. Segundo Fabrício Cardoso Freitas, CEO da Macro Investimentos e membro do Conselho de Administração, o empreendimento poderá contar com energia, água, áreas disponíveis e a estrutura logística do porto, incluindo a possibilidade de conexão ferroviária. Freitas afirmou que o Porto Central já desenvolveu e licenciou 5 gigawatts (GW) de capacidade e destacou a segurança de fornecimento associada ao terminal de Gás Natural Liquefeito (GNL). Para ele, essas condições podem atender à crescente demanda mundial por infraestrutura de processamento de dados. Outro ponto em estudo é a chegada de cabos submarinos de telecomunicações. O porto já possui autorização para receber um cabo, e as tratativas avançam. A proposta é receber, processar e distribuir dados para o mercado brasileiro e também para o exterior. O projeto ainda está em fase de concepção e estruturação. A próxima etapa será definir o modelo do empreendimento, dimensionar infraestrutura e insumos, como energia e água, e prospectar empresas que possam utilizar os futuros data centers.

artigo.texto: Data centers may provide a major economic development opportunity for local communities in Wisconsin, but concerns around water and energy use and potential costs to residents have made them increasingly controversial. A new report from the Wisconsin Policy Forum aims to put those issues — and Wisconsin’s data center debate — into context. Researchers examined tax incentives supporting those projects as well as their energy and water use. Three major data center projects are in varying stages of development in Mount Pleasant, Port Washington and Beaver Dam. Others have been proposed but canceled in DeForest, Greenleaf and Janesville as polling has shown the issue to be unpopular with the public. Communities have ‘significant protections’ under data center incentive deals State law allows qualified developers to avoid paying sales and use tax on most purchases supporting the construction and operation of a data center. The Legislative Fiscal Bureau estimates Wisconsin will lose out on $1.5 billion in sales tax revenues related to data center construction between 2024 and 2028, as well as forgo $369 million annually in sales tax revenue related to data center operations. Wisconsin is one of 38 states that offer tax incentives to data centers. Jason Stein, one of the report’s authors, said without its sales tax exemption, Wisconsin might not have attracted the prominent developments. “I think it’s reasonable to think that a lot of this investment — maybe most of this investment — would not have occurred without the incentive,” he said. The report says the state could “recoup a significant portion of the forgone sales tax revenues” if the sales tax exemption helped attract a significant share of data center investment to Wisconsin. That’s through income and sales taxes paid by construction workers and corporate income taxes paid by construction companies, as well as additional taxes paid by utilities serving data centers. Data centers are also expected to generate increased property tax revenues in the communities hosting them. Researchers reviewed local development agreements in Mount Pleasant, Port Washington and Beaver Dam, as well as proposed deals in communities where developments fell through. They found that, in general, local communities were striking “reasonable deals” that included financial safeguards. Those safeguards often included limits on municipal borrowing, guaranteed property values and incentives tied to project performance, the report said. “If the developer and the community follow through on their agreement and it moves forward as laid out, then those agreements offer substantial protections for the communities,” Stein said. “There are significant protections in each of these deals.” Data centers use water, but Wisconsin water use has declined While much of the public debate around data centers in Wisconsin has centered around water use, policy forum researchers found the bigger challenge is meeting the large electricity demands of those projects while protecting existing ratepayers. That’s because water use in Wisconsin has declined over the past generation as some heavy industry left the state, industrial and residential users became more efficient and electric utilities shifted some energy generation from “water-intensive” coal plants to natural gas and renewable energy, the report said. From 2011 to 2024, water withdrawals in the state fell by more than 500 billion gallons, or almost 24%, according to the report. The three main data center projects in Wisconsin are projected to use less water than the decline in water withdrawals over that period, the report states. “We were on this track to use less and less water because of changes in our society, and maybe this will slow that down somewhat,” Stein said. “But that is a different thing than saying, ‘Oh my gosh, we’re using more water than ever before.’” For example, Racine Water Works, the utility providing water for Microsoft’s data center campus in Mount Pleasant, saw its annual water sales decline by 2.3 billion gallons from 2000 to 2025, according to the report. That’s “more than 250 times” as much water as the 8.4 million gallons annually Microsoft’s data center will use when fully operational, the report states. Electricity demand expected to rise significantly While long-term declines in water use are expected to help offset demand from data centers, Wisconsin’s electricity demand is expected to grow, in large part driven by demand from data centers. Peak demand from all customers on the grid is expected to rise from 14.6 gigawatts in 2024 to 19.9 gigawatts by 2030, the report states. A recent report from state utility regulators found data centers were driving that projected peak demand growth. The report found that the state Public Service Commission modified proposals from We Energies and Alliant Energy establishing rates for data center-scale customers to shield existing residential customers from costs associated with data centers. But it remains to be seen how data centers will affect transmission rates, which are set at the federal level, said Tyler Byrnes, one of the report’s authors. “It’s a little bit easier to do the math on one power plant for one data center, whereas you’re starting to divide up electrons moving across power lines (and) across state lines, so it’s more complicated,” he said. He also said there is not currently an approved data center rate framework for developments of that scale outside the service territories of Alliant Energy and We Energies. He said policymakers may want to consider adopting a statewide framework for electric rates tied to data centers. The report also notes that there are unresolved questions about whether utilities will be able to bring new energy generation and transmission lines online quickly enough to meet the growing demand. This story was originally published by WPR. Originally published by Wisconsin Watch.

artigo.texto: First-ever combined booth showcases the high-throughput FUSION coin cell testing system as AES and MACCOR bring their integrated solution to the battery industry's largest North American event. DETROIT, MI / ACCESS Newswire / October 1, 2026 / Associated Environmental Systems (AES) and MACCOR Inc. will debut the FUSION-08-192-0192, a 192-channel coin cell testing system, at The Battery Show North America. The Battery Show will take place from October 12-15, 2026, at Huntington Place in Detroit, Michigan. For the first time, AES and MACCOR will combine their presence at Booths 3026 and 3126, giving attendees an opportunity to see the system in person. Designed for high-throughput coin-cell research and development, the FUSION-08-192-0192 provides 192 independent testing channels, each capable of up to 1A. The system combines MACCOR battery cycling technology with an AES environmental chamber featuring AES's patented coin cell fixtures, integrated safety systems, pre-wired connections, and unified control via AESONE CONNECT® and the MACCOR Software Suite. FUSION: From Product Launch to the Show Floor AES and MACCOR introduced FUSION in October 2025 as a fully engineered battery-testing system designed to simplify the integration of environmental control and battery cycling. Rather than requiring laboratories to coordinate separate chamber and cycler systems, FUSION brings the major components together as a pre-configured system. The 192-channel configuration expands that approach for high-volume coin cell testing, allowing researchers to run a large number of cells simultaneously under controlled environmental conditions. By engineering the chamber and cycler together, FUSION also reduces the integration effort typically required when separate systems are integrated. "FUSION was created from years of working directly with customers and understanding the challenges involved in integrating battery cyclers with environmental chambers," said Aaron Robinson, Vice President of Sales and Service at AES. "The 192-channel system is a great example of how that approach can increase testing capacity while keeping the overall system integrated and easy to deploy." Built on Experience FUSION builds on AES's decades of industry experience. With more than 5,000 active battery test chambers and more than 200,000 battery testing solutions deployed across the United States, AES understands the demands of real-world battery testing at scale. From high-current applications up to 1,200 amps to the evolving requirements of next-generation battery development, we are constantly pushing the limits of what is possible in environmental test equipment. As battery testing continues to evolve, AES is designing the next generation of solutions to help laboratories test smarter, safer, and more efficiently. The Battery Show North America has become a major gathering for the battery and EV industries. In 2025, the event celebrated its 15th anniversary, attracting more than 21,000 industry professionals and 1,300+ suppliers to Detroit. This year, attendees can see the FUSION-08-192-0192 in person and speak with AES and MACCOR representatives about their battery testing requirements. We are excited to announce that we were named a finalist for the 2026 Battery Show Awards. The awards ceremony will take place on October 13th at 6PM. Stop by Booths 3026 and 3126 at The Battery Show North America, October 12-15, 2026, at Huntington Place in Detroit, Michigan. Learn more about FUSION: AES: associatedenvironmentalsystems.com/fusion-battery-test-system MACCOR: maccor.com/fusion-integrated-systems.html About Associated Environmental Systems Associated Environmental Systems (AES) manufactures environmental test chambers and integrated battery testing equipment from its North Chelmsford, Massachusetts, facility. Founded in 1959, AES is a trusted U.S. manufacturer supporting research and production teams with precise, reliable systems used worldwide. Associated Environmental Systems 15 Wellman Avenue North Chelmsford, MA 01863 USA Sales@associatedenvironmentalsystems.com About MACCOR MACCOR manufactures testing equipment for the battery and energy storage market, serving as a pioneer and global provider of commercial battery test systems. Thousands of MACCOR systems operate worldwide across consumer, automotive, and energy storage applications. artigo.texto: Motta conversou com Vorcaro sobre “sociedade” e PL sobre carbono Presidente da Câmara diz que não há ilícito nas conversas e que os diálogos foram descontextualizados Mensagens obtidas pela Polícia Federal mostram que o presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), manteve conversas com o fundador do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, sobre uma “sociedade” relacionada à compra de um terreno em João Pessoa (PB) e sobre um projeto de lei que trata do mercado de carbono. Em 9 de março de 2024, Motta procurou Vorcaro para tratar da negociação de venda de um terreno na capital paraibana. A conversa se deu no mesmo mês em que Bianca Medeiros, cunhada do presidente da Câmara, contraiu um empréstimo de R$ 22 milhões com o Banco Master para a compra de um terreno em João Pessoa. Mercado de carbono Motta e Vorcaro também conversaram em 19 de novembro de 2024 sobre o projeto de lei que regulamenta o mercado de carbono no Brasil. Trata-se do substitutivo do Senado ao PL 182 de 2024. Na mensagem, Motta menciona uma questão relacionada às seguradoras. A alteração feita pelo Senado e posteriormente modificada na Câmara tratava da possibilidade de seguradoras, além de algumas empresas de previdência e capitalização, comprarem “ativos ambientais” negociados no mercado para compor suas reservas técnicas e provisões. A versão aprovada pelo Senado estipulava que essas empresas destinassem, no mínimo, 0,5% dos recursos a esses ativos. A Câmara retomou a redação anterior, que estabelecia percentual de 1% ao ano. O tema interessava aos negócios de Vorcaro. Em junho de 2026, a PF afirmou que o então banqueiro havia enviado textos de propostas legislativas diretamente ao gabinete do senador Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI). Segundo a investigação, os 2 tinham uma “convergência de interesses ilícitos”. Uma das propostas encaminhadas por Vorcaro ao gabinete do senador tratava justamente da regulamentação do mercado de carbono no país. Outro lado O Poder360 entrou em contato com a defesa de Daniel Vorcaro para saber se gostaria de se manifestar sobre o assunto, mas não teve resposta. A reportagem será atualizada caso a parte envie manifestações a este jornal digital. Procurado pelo Poder360, Motta afirmou, em nota, que mantém diálogo com representantes do empresariado e de outros setores da sociedade e disse não haver ilícito nos diálogos divulgados. O presidente da Câmara também afirmou que as conversas foram descontextualizadas e negou ter atuado em benefício próprio ou de terceiros. Motta informou que pretende apresentar queixa-crime contra o senador Veneziano Vital do Rêgo (MDB-PB). Disse que Veneziano promove calúnia, difamação e divulgação de fake news com finalidade eleitoral. O senador concorre à reeleição e tem como adversário na disputa o pai de Motta, Nabor Wanderley (Republicanos-PB). Sobre o empréstimo contratado com o Banco Master, Motta afirmou que a operação ocorreu quando ainda não eram conhecidas as investigações posteriormente divulgadas sobre a instituição financeira e seu proprietário. Leia a nota de Hugo Motta na íntegra: “Enquanto parlamentar em meu quarto mandato na Câmara dos Deputados, sempre mantive diálogo com os diversos segmentos do empresariado e representantes da sociedade brasileira. Enfatizo que não há nenhum ilícito retratado nos diálogos publicados e repudio a tentativa de atribuir conversas descontextualizadas a qualquer relação de interesse espúrio ou de favorecimento por minha parte. Tenho uma vida limpa, assim como é limpa a minha atuação política nesses 15 anos de vida pública. Informo que estou protocolando queixa-crime contra o senador Veneziano Vital do Rego, diante da série de calúnias, de difamação e produção de fake news que ele tem efetivado contra mim neste período eleitoral. Não permitirei a suspeição de ilícitos promovidos por ele, especialmente com fins eleitoreiros. Como já explicitei anteriormente, o contrato de empréstimo realizado por empresa privada com um banco privado se deu quando não se tinha conhecimento dos fatos e investigações que posteriormente vieram a público sobre o Master e o seu dono. Reitero que confio nos órgãos responsáveis pelas investigações, a quem cabe responder pelas apurações.”

artigo.texto: Read this article in 中文 Français Deutsch Italiano Português Español Nixon Hire agrees exclusive deal on BESS units 02 October 2026 UK rental company Nixon Hire has invested over £1 million in large battery storage units from Infinity Cube Europe. It is part of an agreement that makes Nixon the exclusive UK rental industry user for 18 months, with scope for an extension. This initial order is for 14 units. Six have already been deployed on customer sites, with eight more due later in October. A further four units are expected by the end of the year. The BESS units comprise Infinity Cube’s S Pro, M Pro and L Pro sets, offering 200kW, 300kW and 550kW of energy storage, respectively. The power containers can be linked to create larger battery systems, and each can coordinate the operation of up to three generators, rotating their use. Infinity Cube is based in Singapore and established its European operation earlier this year. Nixon is its first partner in the region’s rental industry. For larger projects Brian Cornett, CEO of Nixon Hire, said the investment builds on the company’s experience with renewable power, extending its battery offer “to larger projects and allowing us to supply higher-capacity power alongside the modular buildings and site accommodation those projects need. “We are proud to be Infinity Cube Europe’s exclusive UK hire partner. The early trials have shown the difference these units can make, and as the fleet expands, we look forward to more customers seeing those benefits on their own sites.” Chris Autey, managing director at Infinity Cube Europe, said he was delighted with the partnership; “[Nixon’s] extensive customer reach, strong relationships and established service infrastructure provide a powerful route to market, ensuring customers can access reliable, high-performance energy storage solutions exactly when they need them. “For customers, the value is clear: proven battery technology delivered through a hire partner they already know and trust.” He said the aim was to “accelerate the adoption of cleaner, more efficient power solutions across a wider range of industries.” Early trial results Nixon Hire, which is based in Newcastle, UK, said early trials included an L Pro supplying power to Nixon equipment including 106 modular office bays, four welfare cabins and washing blocks. Another site saw an M Pro handle the power demand of a tower crane. It said one customer reported saving, in less than a month, more than 13,000 litres of fuel, £20,900 in fuel costs and 33.8 tonnes of CO2 emissions. artigo.texto: Gestão fora de banda em evolução: como simplificar data centers para a era da IA Com o avanço da inteligência artificial, da nuvem e da computação de borda, a infraestrutura de gerenciamento também precisa escalar. Uma arquitetura óptica baseada em PON pode reduzir complexidade, equipamentos e cabeamento, além de centralizar as operações. A expansão da inteligência artificial, dos serviços em nuvem e da computação de borda está acelerando a construção e a modernização de data centers. À medida que esses ambientes crescem, aumenta também a quantidade de equipamentos que precisam ser configurados, monitorados, atualizados e recuperados. Nesse contexto, a rede de gerenciamento fora de banda, conhecida como OOB (Out of Band), deixa de ser um elemento secundário e passa a integrar a estratégia operacional. A rede OOB funciona separadamente da rede principal de dados e permite acesso remoto aos equipamentos mesmo quando há uma falha na infraestrutura de produção. Ela é fundamental para diagnóstico, manutenção e recuperação. No entanto, muitas arquiteturas tradicionais foram construídas com camadas de switches Ethernet, servidores de console, transceptores e grande volume de cabeamento de cobre. Conforme o data center se expande, essa estrutura pode se tornar mais difícil e cara de operar. Por que o modelo tradicional enfrenta limites Cada novo rack pode adicionar equipamentos ativos, portas, fontes de energia, conexões e tarefas de administração. O crescimento pressiona espaço, refrigeração e consumo elétrico, além de aumentar o número de sistemas com ciclos próprios de software, monitoramento e manutenção. Em instalações distribuídas, a dificuldade é ainda maior: as equipes precisam manter políticas e configurações consistentes em vários locais. Hyperscalers foram os primeiros a enfrentar esse problema em grande escala, mas desafios semelhantes agora aparecem em data centers empresariais, instalações de colocation, provedores de nuvem, infraestrutura de IA, ambientes de borda e neoscalers. Esses operadores precisam acelerar implantações, melhorar resiliência e segurança, reduzir custos e apoiar metas de sustentabilidade sem transformar a rede de gerenciamento em uma nova fonte de complexidade. Uma abordagem óptica ponto a multiponto A proposta do DCOM, solução de gerenciamento OOB para data centers da Ciena, é substituir parte da arquitetura ponto a ponto por uma rede óptica passiva, ou PON, baseada em fibra e em conexões ponto a multiponto. A arquitetura foi desenvolvida inicialmente para ambientes de hiperescala e agora foi ampliada para atender diferentes tipos e dimensões de data center. O uso de PON reduz a dependência de camadas tradicionais de agregação, switches OOB e extensas redes de cobre. Com menos elementos ativos na distribuição, a infraestrutura pode ocupar menos espaço, exigir menos energia e simplificar o cabeamento. A mesma abordagem pode ser aplicada tanto à modernização de redes existentes quanto à expansão de novas instalações de IA, nuvem e borda. Um portfólio para diferentes perfis de data center Nem todos os ambientes têm as mesmas exigências de densidade, formato ou expansão. Por isso, a evolução do DCOM inclui opções modulares e fixas. Os chassis 3822, de 1RU, e 3823, de 3RU, operam com a ONU DCOM 3824 e permitem crescimento modular. Para instalações de maior densidade, a plataforma compacta 3826, de 1RU, reúne gerenciamento Ethernet, acesso por console serial e monitoramento de infraestrutura. A variedade de formatos estende as vantagens da arquitetura para empresas, instalações de colocation, sites de borda e outros operadores que não possuem a escala de um hyperscaler, mas enfrentam as mesmas pressões por simplificação e crescimento. O objetivo é oferecer uma base comum capaz de acompanhar diferentes modelos de implantação. Gerenciamento centralizado e ciclo de vida mais simples O valor de uma rede OOB moderna não depende apenas do hardware. O OLT DCOM conecta-se às ONUs, enquanto o DCOM Controller centraliza integração, provisionamento, monitoramento, relatórios, gestão de software e operações de ciclo de vida. O Node Essentials acrescenta visibilidade unificada pela web e administração simplificada. Essa arquitetura transforma dispositivos isolados em uma plataforma operacional mais coesa. Em vez de administrar diversos sistemas independentes, equipes podem aplicar configurações e políticas de forma consistente, acompanhar o ambiente por uma visão comum e racionalizar atualizações. Para organizações com milhares de dispositivos ou múltiplas instalações, a redução da carga operacional pode ser tão relevante quanto a economia física de infraestrutura. Integração, segurança e automação Redes de gerenciamento modernas precisam se integrar às ferramentas existentes. Uma interface northbound permite conectar o DCOM a plataformas de monitoramento, gestão e automação, preservando os fluxos de trabalho de TI. A centralização também apoia provisionamento consistente, monitoramento unificado e controle do ciclo de vida. Como a rede OOB é utilizada em situações críticas, incluindo falhas da rede principal, sua evolução deve considerar segurança e resiliência desde o projeto. Uma plataforma construída especificamente para gerenciamento de data centers ajuda a organizar essas funções sem simplesmente adaptar produtos originalmente destinados a outras finalidades. Eficiência e sustentabilidade no crescimento O aumento de capacidade dos data centers ocorre em um cenário no qual energia, espaço e refrigeração são restrições importantes. Ao reduzir switches OOB tradicionais, camadas de agregação, servidores de console e cabeamento, uma arquitetura óptica mais consolidada pode diminuir consumo e necessidade de refrigeração. Projetos sem ventiladores em determinados componentes também podem contribuir para maior vida operacional. artigo.texto: Data centers vivem "boom" no Brasil e podem dobrar capacidade até 2030 Novas instalações já têm ocupação pré-locada; apesar de crescimento acelerado, setor debate fornecimento de energia Com alta demanda, o Brasil deve dobrar a capacidade de seu mercado de data centers até 2030, com boa parte da nova capacidade já contratada antes mesmo de ficar pronta. Ao todo, dos 660 MW (megawatts) que estão em construção no país, 56% estão pré-locados, segundo levantamento da consultoria JLL. A ocupação dos data centers chegou a 96% no primeiro semestre, deixando uma taxa de 4% para novos clientes. De acordo com o relatório, a baixa disponibilidade deve continuar até 2030, mesmo com a chegada de novos projetos. Desde 2012, a capacidade instalada aumentou mais de seis vezes, com crescimento médio anual de 15%. No primeiro semestre deste ano, o país recebeu 106 MW de nova capacidade, sendo o maior volume registrado. Outros 134 MW estão previstos para entrar em operação ainda no segundo semestre deste ano. Com isso, as entregas de novos data centers devem terminar o ano em níveis recordes, segundo a consultoria. Mesmo com o crescimento constante, o setor ainda enfrenta desafios significativos de infraestrutura, regulação e impacto ambiental. O Redata (Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center), nova lei que prevê um programa de incentivos para o setor no país, foi sancionado no dia 15 pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e deve estimular a instalação e ampliação dos centros de dados no país. Em entrevista à CNN, Tito Costa, CRO da Tecto Data Centers, plataforma de data centers controlada pelo BTG Pactual e ligada à V.tal, prevê que o Brasil dobre a capacidade até o fim de 2027. E que, nos próximos cinco anos, quadruplique o volume. Atualmente a empresa tem sete data centers em operação, sendo três em Fortaleza, um no Rio de Janeiro e três em Barranquilla, na Colômbia. Outros dois centros estão em construção: um em Porto Alegre e outro de 200 MW (cerca de 20% da capacidade brasileira) em Santana de Parnaíba, na Grande São Paulo. Ao todo, o plano de investimentos da companhia é estimado em US$ 2 bilhões, previstos entre 2026 e 2028, para acelerar a expansão na América Latina. "Eu tenho bastante segurança hoje de que é bem provável que a gente, já no ano que vem, dobre a capacidade. E, nos próximos cinco anos, quadruplicar é bastante razoável", afirma Costa. Para o executivo, o "segredo" do aumento na capacidade está na energia que poderia ser gerada, mas cuja produção é restringida, principalmente em usinas eólicas e solares, por meio dos cortes de geração, conhecidos como curtailment, que são impostos pelo ONS (Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico). De acordo com Costa, seriam 4 GW (gigawatts) em curtailment no país, diante de uma capacidade instalada de data centers no Brasil de cerca de 1 GW. Os cortes de energia impostos pelo ONS ocorrem para preservar a segurança e a confiabilidade do sistema elétrico. Entre os motivos estão: a falta de infraestrutura de transmissão, como linhas danificadas ou atrasadas; quando as linhas de transmissão atingem o limite de capacidade e a energia não pode ser escoada; e o excesso de oferta em relação à demanda. Nos dois últimos casos, não há direito a compensação. Para Joísa Dutra, diretora do Ceri-FGV (Centro de Regulação em Infraestrutura) e colunista da CNN Infra, a flexibilidade energética pode ser uma solução, com os data centers sendo projetados para modular seu consumo em até 100 horas por ano — menos de 1% das 8.760 horas anuais — e podendo gerar reduções de tarifas de até 2%. Isso diminuiria a necessidade de investimentos em geração a partir de gás natural. Ela defende que a adoção antecipada de boas práticas e protocolos é essencial para que esses investimentos sejam vistos não como problemas, mas como parte da solução — tanto para o setor elétrico quanto para os demais sistemas de recursos com os quais se relacionam. "Flexibilidade é tudo que a gente quer neste momento, onde o setor elétrico navega para essa descentralização, para essa produção de mais eletricidade a partir de solar e eólica", destaca a colunista. Além do consumo de energia, Joísa chama a atenção para o impacto desses projetos sobre outros recursos naturais, como água, minerais e terra, citando o projeto de data center na região de Pecém, no Ceará, que tem o TikTok como um dos membros da parceria e está localizado em uma área com estresse hídrico. Para ela, a adoção antecipada de boas práticas e protocolos é essencial para que esses investimentos sejam vistos não como problemas, mas como parte da solução — tanto para o setor elétrico quanto para os demais sistemas de recursos relacionados. Ainda segundo o executivo, o Brasil está super bem posicionado e está muito perto de explodir o mercado, tendo a IA como uma outra frente de expansão. Na avaliação dele, assim como a demanda americana, que tem superado as projeções nos últimos, o movimento também deve chegar ao Brasil em breve. Para atrair a demanda que está fora do país, Costa defende a redução no custo dos data centers e dos serviços de nuvem. "Cerca de 40% do workload brasileiro roda nos Estados Unidos, [o crescimento] depende de eu fazer o datacenter mais barato para a cloud no Brasil ficar mais barata, ou tão barata quanto a lá de fora, para o usuário usar aqui", pondera. Em relação ao Redata, Costa afirma que o projeto reduz a barreira tributária sobre equipamentos e aproxima o Brasil dos custos internacionais, mas ainda assim estima que construir e implantar um data center em solo nacional custa entre 15% e 20% mais, além de defender a discussão do ICMS no setor. “A gente deve estar 15% a 20% acima. Tem uma discussão do ICMS que o Redata não endereça, e é um tema que a gente precisa endereçar." Setor busca acelerar investimentos Ainda segundo Joísa Dutra, o setor busca acelerar os investimentos de forma mais eficiente, buscando alianças internacionais, ao mencionar o lanlamento da AI Energy Management All

artigo.texto: The Elements of Innovation Discovered Metal Tech News - September 29, 2026 An up to $75 million Pentagon grant awarded to Amprius Technologies to reconfigure an electric vehicle battery production line to one that produces high-energy-density silicon-anode lithium-ion cells for drones highlights an emerging shift in the battery market. Since the introduction of the Nissan LEAF and Chevrolet Volt in 2010, electric vehicles have increasingly driven lithium-ion battery demand. Automakers have shifted among cathode chemistries to balance cost, range, safety, and performance, including the growing use of lower-cost but less energy-dense lithium iron phosphate. Graphite, however, has remained the predominant material on the anode side of both battery types. Drones, robotics, and more compact transportation such as e-bikes are changing the battery equation. Unlike passenger EVs, where cost per kilowatt-hour is a major consideration, drones and other weight-sensitive technologies place a premium on packing more energy into every kilogram and cubic inch of battery. Amprius Technologies is targeting that market with lithium-ion batteries that replace much of the graphite traditionally used on the anode side with silicon, an abundant element capable of storing substantially more lithium than graphite. The challenge is that silicon expands dramatically as it absorbs lithium during charging, which can cause conventional silicon particles to crack and degrade after repeated cycles. Amprius has developed two primary battery platforms to overcome this problem. Designed to deliver maximum energy density, its SiMaxx technology uses a high-purity silicon nanowire anode that provides room for the silicon to expand and contract during charging and discharging while maintaining electrical contact. The company's SiCore platform uses a proprietary silicon-carbon anode material designed to balance high energy density with power, cycle life, manufacturability, and cost. Amprius introduced a second-generation SiCore cell in September capable of being manufactured on conventional lithium-ion battery production equipment. This ability to produce high-energy silicon-anode batteries on existing equipment is central to the Pentagon-backed project. To explain the energy-density advantage in an easy-to-visualize way, Amprius CEO Tom Stepien compares conventional graphite batteries with drip coffee and the company's silicon-anode batteries with espresso. Both can provide roughly the same caffeine, but espresso fits that dose into a much smaller volume. Likewise, an Amprius battery can provide a similar amount of energy in a smaller and lighter package, or significantly more energy within the same weight and space constraints. For a drone, that can mean longer flight time, greater range, or room for additional payload. The U.S. Department of War's Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program has awarded Amprius up to $75 million to bring that technology into high-volume domestic production. Under what the company calls Project acCELLerate, Amprius plans to reconfigure an existing U.S.-based EV battery production line operated by an unnamed major South Korean battery manufacturer to produce advanced silicon-anode pouch cells for unmanned aerial systems. The converted line is expected to be operating by early 2028 with capacity to produce 12 million Amprius cells annually. Amprius estimates the conversion will cost roughly $100 million, including in-kind investments from the company and its South Korean manufacturing partner. "Our technology, combined with the U.S. manufacturing prowess of our South Korean manufacturing partner, positions us to accelerate adoption of standardized, high-performance pouch cells in a fast-growing market," said Stepien. The decision to convert an EV battery production line to manufacture cells for military drones also underscores a changing lithium-ion battery market. EVs created enormous demand for batteries that balance range, longevity, safety, and affordability. Drones, advanced aviation, robotics, light electric vehicles, and other mobile technologies are creating markets where reducing battery weight and volume can be worth paying a premium. This is particularly true for aircraft, where every pound devoted to batteries is a pound that cannot be used for payload, and every improvement in energy density can translate directly into longer flight times. The Pentagon-backed production line could also provide Amprius with the manufacturing scale needed to expand further into commercial drones, robots, e-bikes, electric aviation, and other applications where packing more energy into a smaller space carries a premium. And if higher production volumes and manufacturing efficiencies lower the cost of silicon-anode batteries, the market for the technology could broaden further. That could eventually open the door for EVs and other transportation systems capable of carrying drip-coffee-sized energy in an espresso-sized package.

artigo.texto: World’s largest single-location battery energy storage system (BESS) Ahmedabad, 01 October 2026: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL), India’s largest renewable energy company, has expanded its operational Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity to 6.63 gigawatt-hours (GWh) at Khavda, Gujarat, from 3.55 GWh in June 2026. AGEL now accounts for more than 50% of India’s operational BESS capacity of about 12.6 GWh. This milestone consolidates Khavda’s position as the world’s largest operational battery energy storage installation at a single location, with 6.63 GWh of operational capacity. AGEL achieved the 6.63 GWh milestone within 14 months of commencing on-site BESS construction at Khavda, Gujarat with this latest capacity addition being commissioned in just 10 months from the start of its construction. The BESS is integrated with AGEL’s renewable energy (RE) development at Khavda, where the company is developing a 30 GW RE plant across 538 square kilometers of barren land. The AGEL 6.63 GWh BESS can store enough clean energy to power around two million homes a day, and support peak electricity demand of cities like Nagpur, Patna or Vizag for several hours. This BESS capacity at Khavda is equivalent to battery storage capacity of more than 150,000 mid-sized EVs and can store enough energy daily to meet almost twice the Delhi Metro's estimated daily electricity requirement, underscoring the unprecedented scale of the installation. The scale-up to 6.63 GWh strengthens the integration of renewable energy into the grid by enabling clean power to be stored and dispatched when required. Mr Sagar Adani, Executive Director, Adani Green Energy, said, “Reaching 6.63 GWh of operational battery storage in just 14 months is a significant milestone for AGEL and India’s clean energy transition. At this scale, storage can make renewable power firmer, more reliable and dispatchable when the grid needs it. As India’s power demand grows, we will continue to scale energy storage solutions, both, battery and pumped storage to support a more resilient, lower-carbon grid.” Photo: World’s largest Battery Energy Storage at Khavda, Gujarat where Adani Green Energy is also developing the World’s largest RE plant Advanced project controls, digital monitoring systems, agile construction management practices, and strategic partnerships with leading global BESS OEMs enabled adherence to aggressive project timelines while maintaining stringent quality and safety standards. The deployment serves as a benchmark for large-scale energy storage execution and operations, supporting India's energy transition through reliable and scalable storage infrastructure. The BESS uses lithium-ion battery technology, integrated with an Energy Management Systems (EMS) and automated telemetry to manage charging and discharging, optimise system performance and support grid services. Battery storage can improve grid stability, manage peak demand, reduce energy curtailment and enable renewable power to be delivered when required. AGEL is on track to add over 10 GWh of BESS capacity in FY 2026-27 and is targeting 50 GWh of storage capacity over the next 5 years. The company is also pursuing pumped storage projects (PSPs) as part of its broader strategy to build large-scale, firm and dispatchable renewable power capacity. About Adani Green Energy Limited: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) is India’s largest and one of the leading renewable energy companies in the world enabling the clean energy transition. AGEL develops, owns, and operates utility scale grid-connected solar, wind, hybrid and energy storage solutions. AGEL currently has an operating renewable portfolio of 20.76 GW and 6.63 GWh of battery energy storage, the largest in India, spread across 12 states. The company has set a target of achieving 50 GW by 2030 aligned to India’s decarbonization goals. AGEL is focused on leveraging technology to reduce the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) in pursuit of enabling large-scale adoption of affordable clean energy. AGEL is developing the world’s largest renewable energy plant (30 GW) on barren land at Khavda, Gujarat, covering 538 square kilometers, an area five times larger than Paris. AGEL’s operating portfolio is certified as water positive, single-use plastic free and zero waste-to-landfill, a testament to the company’s commitment to power sustainable growth. artigo.texto: China plans to launch solid-state battery production by 2030 — OilPrice China plans to begin commercial production of solid-state batteries by 2030, reduce their cost and improve their performance. This was reported by OilPrice, citing a statement by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The ministry said that over the next five years, the new-type battery industry will be in a critically important period of technological renewal. The ministry called for making use of strategic opportunities related to technological and industrial innovation. Bet on new materials The plan provides for work on new materials for electrodes, electrolytes and other components of solid-state batteries. The publication notes that electrolytes are currently one of the vulnerable components of this technology. The plan also covers sodium and flow batteries, which are seen as possible alternatives to lithium-ion batteries. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram. Solid-state batteries may have higher energy density, charge faster, last longer and be safer than lithium-ion batteries. At the same time, their large-scale adoption is hindered by high costs and technical malfunctions that have complicated development for years. BYD’s plans and market growth China already dominates the global lithium-ion battery market and seeks to strengthen its position in the next-generation technology segment. BYD has also previously stated its intention to begin mass production of solid-state batteries for electric vehicles by 2030. At the same time, the company plans to continue using lithium-ion batteries as well. According to Global Times data cited by OilPrice, China’s solid-state battery market amounted to about $42.5 million last year and could grow to $384.8 million by 2030. At the same time, China is already facing excess production capacity in the lithium-ion battery segment for electric vehicles and energy storage systems.

artigo.texto: Oklahoma lawmakers hold interim study on benefits, costs of data center growth OKLAHOMA CITY (KOKH) — As residents across the state deal with the possibility of data centers coming to their communities, Oklahoma lawmakers held an interim study to determine the benefits and impacts of data center development in the Sooner State. This week, Rep. Mark Chapman, R-Broken Arrow, led an interim study examining the benefits, costs, and long-term impacts of data center developments in Oklahoma. Chapman said he wanted give lawmakers an opportunity to look at the issue from multiple perspectives. "For the past year, I've heard a lot of discussions and concerns about data centers, and I felt it was time to lay the cards on the table and look at this issue as objectively as we can," Chapman said. "There are potential opportunities, but there are also legitimate questions about infrastructure, resources and the effects on communities. We need to understand what communities may be saying yes to, what they may be saying no to and what safeguards need to be in place." Much of the study focused on how data centers affect utility planning and local resources. Experts discussed the large power needs of newer facilities, safeguards intended to keep project costs with the customers creating them and how water use can vary. They also discussed ways to better connect existing resources so communities can more easily evaluate proposed projects and understand potential impacts. Chapman said he will continue reviewing information gathered during the study to determine whether additional legislative action is warranted.

artigo.texto: NESTA EDIÇÃO. Um mês após aprovação no Congresso Nacional, gás no Redata segue sem definição. Lula promete distribuidora estatal se for reeleito. Coreia do Sul vai investir em projetos de energia nos EUA, inclusive no Alasca. Hidrelétricas reversíveis, baterias e usinas a resíduos entram no calendário de leilões do setor elétrico. EDIÇÃO APRESENTADA POR: Estados intensificam articulação em favor do gás no Redata Os estados intensificaram, nos últimos dias, a mobilização em favor do reconhecimento do gás natural como alternativa energética elegível como fonte de baixa emissão incentivada pelo programa de incentivos para a atração de data centers, o Redata. - Na quarta (30/9), o Fórum Nacional de Secretários Estaduais de Minas e Energia (FNSME) pediu ao presidente Lula (PT) a abertura de um diálogo institucional com os estados antes da conclusão da regulamentação e a inclusão do gás como fonte incentivada. - O FNSME afirma que cada estado tem vocações energéticas diferentes e que o programa deve preservar condições isonômicas na atração dos investimentos em data centers. Outras manifestações na mesma linha ocorreram nos últimos dias: os governos do Rio Grande do Sul e do Paraná enviaram ofícios ao presidente Lula esta semana. - Antes, os governos do Amazonas e Sergipe também já haviam solicitado formalmente a inclusão do gás na regulamentação do Redata. Na visão do investidor… Em entrevista à agência eixos, o CEO da Elea Data Centers, Alessandro Lombardi, reconheceu que o gás natural pode contribuir para o atendimento aos data centers, sobretudo como fonte de reserva em situações de interrupção do fornecimento elétrico, embora prefira que os incentivos estivessem vinculados exclusivamente à energia renovável. Confira na entrevista - Além disso, a Elea afirma que seguirá à risca os procedimentos de licenciamento ambiental de seu data center em Belém (PA) e sustenta que o empreendimento não comprometerá o fornecimento de energia aos consumidores locais. - O CEO da Prumo Logística, Rogério Zampronha, também defende o reconhecimento do gás natural como alternativa elegível. A companhia opera o Porto do Açu, que tem três clusters de data centers em negociação, sendo que dois projetos aguardam a promulgação do Redata para retomar o ritmo. A expectativa era que o decreto regulamentador do programa fosse assinado pelo presidente Lula até segunda passada (28/9). Até o fechamento desta edição, o texto não havia sido divulgado. - O governo segue dividido sobre o tema. O Ministério da Fazenda, responsável pelo desenho do programa, tem pressionado para que o gás fique de fora das fontes incentivadas, enquanto o ministro de Minas e Energia, Alexandre Silveira (PSD) defende a inclusão do energético na política. Mais detalhes no site: O projeto de lei que cria o Redata foi aprovado há exatamente um mês no Senado Federal. - A brecha para a entrada do gás natural como fonte complementar no programa surgiu a partir de uma emenda de redação. O texto priorizava energias renováveis e “limpas”, mas durante a tramitação no Congresso este último termo foi substituído por “de baixa emissão”. E fique de olho na agenda do gás. De olho na seca.
